Question: Rahul has demanded JPC probe into Stock market scam blaming Modi, Shah and FM behind it as investors have lost 30 lakh crores. What is your opinion on this?
Answer: Stock Market Scam: I have been a keen follower of electoral politics since 1977 when Congress went out of power for the first time at the national level. I have been a stock market learner too from the same year. This question combines both the fields, so I am tempted to answer. What happened over last 1 week?: Markets were uncertain before the Lok Sabha elections concluded. There were talks of 400 + seats for NDA and towards the end of the long drawn out elections, there was some fatigue in that theme and in the market too. Most people, including the stock market players believed that BJP would get a majority, a decent majority on its own to form the government for a third consecutive term. Exit polls by various TV channels added to that belief. Home Minister Amit Shah told in some election rally that markets are bound to go up after the BJP/NDA victory. So the smart investor should invest in the market. (Not these exact words but something along the same theme) Exit polls happened on June 01, Saturday and market went through the roof on June 03, Monday. On June 04, as the results were pouring in and BJP was not getting the anticipated results, market euphoria of Monday turned into despair (it happens quite regularly in the market) and the index crashed in a big way. This is what made Rahul Gandhi say that investors lost Rs. 30 lakh crores. Did they actually lose?: Some traders surely lost in a big way as their positions built over previous few days went into a tailspin and losses had to be booked. Trading is such a beast. It devours profits and turns them into a loss in no time. But then, traders knew the risks. As things settled down, it became clear that BJP is coming back to power as NDA for the third term, market recovered and by Friday, June 07, 2024 had made another record high for both NIFTY and SENSEX. See how it happened: Where did the investor lose money? Those who stayed put for 2–3 days, recouped whatever notional loss was there. There was no loss of Rs. 30 lakh crores to investors as claimed by Rahul Gandhi. Why did Rahul Gandhi say it?: Mostly politicians make false statements and accusations on each other. This is common to all parties. Rahul Gandhi in his new found confidence after improved results in the elections, probably thought that he has got another strong point against Modi- Shah. He will have to look elsewhere for any strong point. This point is not worth a small debate, what to speak of a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Why should we waste public money in useless discussions which are bound to result in nothing. Was Amit Shah wrong in speaking about stock market in his election speech?: Maybe, to a very small extent. But then election speeches are all bluster and rhetoric. Nobody actually means what they speak. We had lot of other nonsense like Mangalsutra, Buffaloes, Khata Khat, Cash in Tempos . If public can see through all that, why would they bother about what Amit Shah says about stock market. Yes, few people lost money: So what. These people are not the poor people who need hand holding by the government or opposition leaders. They took an investment/trading decision based on their reading of the market. It went wrong and the money was lost. It happens everyday to the traders in stock market. Neither Mr. Modi nor Rahul Gandhi care for these traders. It was just to score a point over Modi-Shah, which did not amount to much. To Conclude: Market has a mind of its own. It reacts to political events in a volatile manner but eventually everything evens out. Yesterday, oath taking and ministry formation was done. This is the market reaction today: Today also, NIFTY index made a new record high at 23411.90 and then climbed down from that level. Highs and lows are daily occurrences in the market. Only the volatility is very high on election results kind of days. On Saturday, June 08, I had written this answer: Pramod Kumar's answer to Why is Congress happy despite the loss? Excerpt from that answer: There is nothing to be inquired into. No wrongs have been committed. Rahul Gandhi should focus on things other than stock market. Market will go higher or lower without interference from the politicians. Occasional positive nudges are okay for the market but nothing more is needed. These were my views on the question posed. Thanks for reading.

Question: Why is Congress happy despite the loss?
Answer: Elections 2024 are over. NDA with BJP as the major party (240 seats) is forming the government with Prime Minister Sh. Narendra Modi taking the oath of office for the third term tomorrow on June 09, 2024. Congress led by Sh Rahul Gandhi won 99 seats in this election and is a distant second to BJP. Still the party is happy. Why the Congress party is happy despite the loss?: Reason 1: Party had won just 44 seats in 2014. In 2019, the performance was similar with 52 seats. In 2024, there is surely improvement with 99 seats secured. A gain of 47 seats. That is something to be happy about. Reason 2: Rahul Gandhi contested from two seats, Wayanad in Kerala and Rae Bareli in Uttar Pradesh,. Here is the result of Rae Bareli: He won the seat with a big margin securing 66.2% of the polled votes. This in Uttar Pradesh where he had lost in Amethi constituency in 2019. In Wayanad too, he emerged a winner. And this man was called Pappu and Shehzada by his adversaries never giving him any respect. But the public verdict went in Rahul Gandhi’ favour. The same Uttar Pradesh electorate of Varanasi, where Prime Minister Sh. Narendra Modi won for the third time, gave only 54.2% votes to him. A nobody like Ajay Rai of Congress got 40.7% votes. That is a reason to be happy. Reason 3: Sometime people get happiness from their own results. At times, they derive happiness from failure of others. BJP had 303 seats in the outgoing Lok Sabha. That number is reduced to 240 now. When your main adversary loses 63 seats and you gain 47 seats, that is a reason to be happy. Reason 4: With 99 seats, Congress Party will be the official opposition party in the Lok Sabha, s status which the party could not get earlier due to poor results in 2014 and 2019. For most of the debates in the house, time is allotted based on the party’s strength in the house. Congress party will now get more debating time and opportunity to put forth their view. This too is a reason to be happy. Reason 5: The party fared very badly in Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. Anyway, that was a forgone conclusions even before a single vote was cast. Getting 1 seat from Gujarat is actually a surprise. But the party did well in Haryana and Maharashtra. This momentum is to be carried into assembly elections in these two states and it is quite feasible to be in a position to form the government there. That is another reason for being happy. This man, ridiculed and mocked continuously over last 10 years, plodded on relentlessly making quite a few mistakes also, along that journey but eventually the electorate rewarded him with victory in both the seats he contested. And much more resounding victory in Rae Bareli than the win secured by the Prime Minister in Varanasi, a constituency which he has represented for two terms previously. Rahul Gandhi is no longer a Pappu. He may yet be derided by BJP, but he is respected by his allies and has the trust of the electorate. That is one very big reason to be HAPPY. What is there not to be happy?: Public has not expressed enough confidence in the party and its allies to give them the mandate of forming the government. More hard work needs to be done over next 5 years. Rahul Gandhi is prone to make unsubstantiated and meaningless allegations just for saying something against Modi. His recent utterances about stock market crash on the result day causing loss of Rs. 30 Lakh Crores to the investors is one such ridiculous talk. It does not take much time for happiness to turn into sorrow in politics. A strong opposition is good for democracy. Congress and I.N.D.I. alliance must strive to provide that strong and effective opposition rather than making half baked attempts at government formation through defections. Congress has few reasons to be happy but lot more to be worried about over next 5 years. The people have spoken. They made every party happy except few like BJD in Odisha, AIADMK in Tamilnadu, YSRCongress in Andhra Pradesh, BRS in Telagana, BSP in Uttar Pradesh and probably one or two more which I do not recall at this time. I hope this answers the question.

Question: If JDU and TDP withdraw their support to BJP, shall the Modi 3.0 fall?
Answer: Why the hurry? Modi 3.0 - these terms are in vogue now though people from the heartland of the nation do not connect with the term, is yet to begin. Why do we have to ask questions about the fall of a government even before it has taken oath? Is it pessimism or just passing time? Well, whatever it is, here are my two bits. Past governments lasting full term without majority: P V Narasimha Rao (1991–96), Atal Bihari Vajpayee (1999–2004) , Manmohan Singh ( 2004–2014) completed full terms as Prime Ministers while not enjoying a majority for their party. They all faced problems of withdrawal of support, no confidence motions, turmoil within the party in case of P V Narasimha Rao but the governments completed full terms. What is different now?: If these two gentlemen withdraw support? They may not do it immediately. Right now their concern is to get good bargain for their support. Naidu needs central government funding for Andhra Pradesh. So does Bihar. Both are looking for Special Category Status. Special states among other states. Will BJP concede that? Or these states may get larger share of funds without the tag of special category. At some point in future, secularism will raise its head. TDP has promised Haj Subsidy and 4% reservation for Muslims. Nitish had withdrawn support from BJP questioning Modi’s secular credentials in the past. These issues will come up maybe a year from now. BJP will have to tackle these? Manmohan Singh was a political novice. Narasimha Rao and Vajpayee were masters in managing conflicting thought process. If all these people could manage to complete their full terms without having a majority in the Lok Sabha, present incumbent can surely do it. With 10 years of governance and facing a myriad of problems, Sh Narendra Modi is experienced enough to ride through any real or perceived crisis situation that may come up. It is not to say that Naidu or Nitish or both or any of the other allies will not ditch BJP at any time. They will surely do at some point when their interest is compromised or BJP may ditch them if pushed to the brink. Managing a coalition is not easy but Mr Modi should surmount the challenges posed. That is what the top post calls for. Face the challenges and come out on top. Interesting times ahead. It is not MODI SARKAR, it is NDA SARKAR. Managing a coalition and running the government would be a humbling experience for the BJP. It is good for the party and good for the nation. For the present, let us look forward to swearing in of the new government. Nobody is withdrawing support anytime soon. I am not a fan of Mr Modi but would surely like to see him as Prime Minister once again. Prime Minister in the true sense of parliamentary democracy - First Among Equals - not like a monarch not to be questioned. Long live Indian Democracy with all its quirks and twists. Thanks for reading.

Question: Will Nitish Kumar and Chandrababu Naidu ditch Narendra Modi and accept the India Alliance proposal to join them to form the next UPA government once again?
Answer: I am writing this on June 06, 2024. Yesterday, both Nitish Kumar and Chandrababu Naidu pledged their support to NDA and Sh. Narendra Modi as the leader of NDA coalition. For the present, neither of them is joining with the INDIA bloc to form a UPA government once again. But politics is the game of the impossible and we can always find strange bedfellows. Let us analyze the two supporting parties: Telugu Desam Party (TDP) - Chandrababu Naidu: He was very important member of NDA in Atal Ji’s government. He insisted upon getting the Lok Sabha speaker post for TDP and got it - GMC Balayogi was the speaker. Bill gates went to Hyderabad first and to New Delhi afterwards. His support was crucial to NDA at that time and it is crucial now. He will look for his interests all of which will be Andhra Pradesh specific. BJP may have problems with some of those. For example, Naidu’s promise of 4% reservation for Muslims. BJP ally Chandrababu Naidu promises 4% Muslim reservation in Andhra Sh. Narendra Modi has spoken from every platform that BJP is against religion based reservation and it will never happen under BJP rule. How will they resolve it? Will BJP swallow its pride and accept what Naidu does? Or BJP will act differently at state level and center? We shall know the answer in few months. Special status for Andhra Pradesh may not be a problem in principle. Trouble will come when it is time to disburse the promised funds. It can be a very serious bone of contention. TDP does not depend on BJP in the state assembly but BJP depends on TDP in Lok Sabha. Naidu will take every advantage of it and he will not be wrong in doing that. Will he be loyal to NDA? He was not loyal to Sh N T Ramarao , his Father in law and founder of TDP. Why to expect loyalty for Modi Ji? He will surely ditch BJP when it suits him. Janata Dal (United) - JD(U) - Nitish Kumar Nitish Kumar was a prominent member of Atal Ji’s led NDA. He is among the prominent turncoats of the recent times having changed loyalty multiple times. In 2013, he left NDA because Modi was projected as BJP candidate for the Prime Minister post for the elections to be held in 2014. His reasoning was that Modi was communal . Today, we have same Nitish Kumar endorsing Modi as Prime Minister in 2024. What happened to being communal? For Nitish Kumar, it has been all about jumping from one side to the other based on his understanding of benefits at that point of time. Surely, the support of such a master of flip flops can not be taken for granted. And the temporary support too must have a costly price tag details of which will not be shared with the public. To Summarize: All is well at present. Few months down the line, we may see some stress in the relationship. Alliances need some give and take. All would depend on how much BJP is willing to give. All the best for the NDA coalition and for the citizens of the nation.

Question: Did anyone lose any amount in a mutual fund when they invested more than 5 years?

For their expertise, mutual funds charge a fee from the investors. Over long term, mutual funds normally give reasonable returns. Question is about a likely loss over 5 year time period. Let us see how a loss is possible and if that has happened in the past. Let us have a look how NIFTY index has moved since inception in 1996: Index has gained 2349% since 1996. That is why we are willing to pay their fee. When they are not able to do better than the index, they keep quiet. What else can they do? They operate in the same market like all of us. Nobody has yet found the key to eternal profitability, all the big names and mutual funds are no different. They also have flat and losing time spans. Let us have a look at two such events in the past. Crash of 2008: NIFTY had gone above 6000 for the first time in January 2008. Then, the crash happened. In October 2008, NIFTY had gone below 2200 level. And it took some time to get back to 6000 again. People investing in 2004–2005 would have seen very good gains in the beginning of 2008. And then seen those gains turn into a loss as every stock crashed. They became profitable again after 2010. Covid-19 Dip in March 2020: I remember the day when SENSEX hit 30000 for the first time. Occasional declines will happen from time to time, key is to stay invested. Thanks for reading.

Question: What are your thoughts on the scandal involving Electoral Bonds in India?
Answer: My thoughts on the scandal involving Electoral Bonds in India: The last few days have been entertaining. I do not watch news on TV. So I must have certainly missed the biggest entertainment package of 2024 -the talk shows on Electoral Bonds. Who got how much and from whom? But Quora too can be entertaining. There are questions and answers supporting BJP, against BJP, twisting the available facts to suit the narrative of the person writing. All those posts make for good entertainment. There is no scandal. Scandal is when something is done against the prevalent norms. Collection of money by the political parties is nothing new. Earlier it used to be in cash. Things changed a little when Electoral Bonds came into picture after 2017. It is not that cash went out. Cash is more anonymous. Electoral Bonds were supposed to be anonymous but Supreme Court of India changed that by declaring the scheme - UNCONSTITUTIONAL. That means, the secrecy part of the bonds is taken away and people get to know who gave money to which party. This is what is happening over last one week. We are enjoying the circus. There are some new characters nobody thought off. There are significant names missing. Does it mean those missing names did not contribute to the election funds of various parties? Neither the political parties or the business houses are epitomes of virtue and purity. They would have just done it through cash like it was always done. No proof, no pointing fingers, everything is fine. The unexpected names will be in the news for a few days and then forgotten. We have got more entertainment coming in the form of Lok Sabha Elections. Why it is no scandal?: Scandal is something which shocks and jolts us. We, then look for avoiding such incidents in future. There is shame or sorrow or pity involved with a scandal when we look at it from the perpetrator side or the victim side. Did we see any political party being ashamed? Did we see any acceptance of wrongdoing by a political party? Did we see any donor regretting their contribution and pledging to avoid such donations in future? Not at all. When there is no shame, no acceptance of being wrong, no sense of remorse, there is no scandal. This is the accepted behaviour from political class. No party can claim high moral ground. All are same. It does not matter: Let us be practical. I asked my 85 year old mother whether this electoral bond thing will change her voting preference? She looked at me like I had lost my mind. I asked the same question from my wife. She said - what is this all about. I got better things to do than this nonsense. So 2 out of 3 voters in my house do not care. I talked to about 10 people, well informed, young and old and it did not matter for 9 of them. Believe it or not, this issue is not going to impact the coming election at all, TV talks and Quora posts notwithstanding. We are like this only.

Question: Why does HDFC Bank stock keep falling, and when will stock recover?
Answer: Good question. Let us first look at how HDFCBANK stock price performed over last one year. The price was 1460.75 on March 12, 2024, down 6.87% in a year. The lowest price during 52 weeks was Rs. 1363.55 on February 14, 2024. On its own, the decline of 6.87% is not alarming, but the market has been in a sustained bull run in this period. The benchmark index NIFTY 50 has gained 30% in the same period. HDFCBANK is the stock with the highest weight among NIFTY 50 stocks. Had this stock also kept pace with the index, we would have been looking at 23000 level for NIFTY. Why the decline?: Analysts on business channels keep on feeding us multiple reasons for everyday gains or losses in a stock price. If we add up all their reasons, it amounts to very entertaining nonsense. Let us get practical - a stock falls when big investors move out of it. You and I selling 20 shares or 200 shares does not have any impact. But an institutional investor reducing the holding by 2 Million shares makes the price go down. So we conclude that institutional investors are moving out. Why? To them, the last quarter results were not impressive. Net interest margin (NIM) is lower than the previous quarter. It may not mean too much to a retail investor but to big institutions it is a sign that things are not well. So they start pulling out their capital. This is what happened in case of HDFCBANK. On the other hand, there are those investors who believe that the performance would improve in future. These people are buying, their buying has brought the stock price to the current level. Further move will be decided by the institutions which were selling. This is a tug of war which keeps on going all the time. In the case of HDFCBANK, this round went to SELLERS. Merger with HDFC: Last year when the merger with HDFC happened, the stock price shot up. The usual talk - combined synergies, bigger customer base, lower serving costs, access to easy deposits — was the explanation for the surge in price at that time. All explanations go wrong when the selling starts. This is what India Today reported on the day stock made the 52 week low: With such a big decline in NIM, 4% to 3.4%, price was bound to go down. And it really did. Other Housing Finance Companies: Over last one year, PNB Housing Finance, India Bulls Housing Finance, REPCO Home Finance share prices have moved lower in a market which is up 30%. LIC Housing Finance has done better with some gain, but that gain is also not much compared to overall market gain. This implies that Housing Loan companies have not done well over last one year and a big part of HDFCBANK is the former HDFC which was a housing loan company. Recovery from the low: Well, part recovery has already happened. Further up move is possible if the Housing Loan part of the company performs well and the institutional investors place their trust again in the stock. Still, it is one of the good banking stocks and one should not get out in panic. Market leaders are leaders for a reason. Thanks for reading.

Question: What do you think about the results of the 5 Indian state elections of March 2022?
Answer: What do you think about the results of 5 Indian State elections of March 2022?: The people have voted. Big change happened in Punjab where AAP ( Aam Aadmi Party ) won a thumping majority and will be forming the government. Big guns of INC as well as SAD lost their seats to newcomers of AAP. It is a complete change. Next 5 years will be a test for the new government. In Uttar Pradesh, BJP has retained power. In the euphoria of victory, the following facts are being ignored: (a) Number of seats has come down to 255 from 302 in the previous elections. This is a loss of 57 seats. (b) Deputy Chief Minister, Keshav Prasad Maurya lost his seat. Another 10 Ministers also lost in this election. (c) SP ( Samajwadi Party ) led by Akhilesh Yadav, won 111 seats improving the party’s tally by 64. Most of these seats have come at the expense of BJP. In a winner take all system, party that wins gets all the accolades. But let us not forget that 11 Ministers losing the elections suggests some anti -incumbency. UP Election Results 2022: Keshav Prasad Maurya, 10 other ministers in Yogi Adityanath govt lose their seats In other 3 states BJP has done well to retain power though Chief Minister losing from his constituency in Uttarakhand is a dampener in an otherwise good victory. Does it change anything?: Contrary to the brouhaha in the media, nothing changes or nothing has changed. Congress has lost Punjab. BJP did not gain anything there. BJP won the other states where it was already in power. In UP, it has come back with a reduced majority. In fact, nothing is achieved accept maintaining status quo. It is good for democracy. All India Picture after these results: India has developed into a true Federal democracy over the years. The hegemony of one or two parties has become a thing of the past. After counting the results for these 5 state elections, the ALL INDIA position of state assemblies is like this: Total — 4025 Seats BJP — 1432 Seats INC —- 636 Seats Other parties — 1957 Seats BJP holds 35.57% seats in Assembly Constituencies all over India. Compare it to the position in Lok Sabha — 301 out of 543 which is 55%. Congress still holds 15.8% seats in state assemblies across India. But it is other parties with base in select states that get the best results. We have got — YSR Congress in Andhra, TRS is Telangana, DMK in Tamilnadu, Left Front in Kerala, BJD in Odisha, AITC in West Bengal where both BJP and Congress are not significant. This tells us that state elections are entirely different from Lok Sabha elections. People vote for what is best for them and get it right most of the time. I think, they got it right this time too.

Question: Do you think the Indian stock market is overheated?
Answer: Do you think that Indian stock market is overheated?: I may think that the market is overheated. Does it matter? Who cares for what I think? Market runs on flow of money. If more money chases few stocks, prices tend to go up. The money chases one group of stocks at one time, then goes for another group. We see IT stocks soaring high one day while banks are going down. Next day, the roles get reversed. Well, let us talk about the heat. My readers know me for my short trades and PUT buying trades. That probably makes me bearish about the market. My preferences notwithstanding, I do not think that he market is overheated at this point of time. Let us have a look at NIFTY P/E (Price to Earnings) ratio: It was 26.25 on August 31, 2021. This is not too high a number. An year ago, P/E ratio was much higher: It was 32.29. What does it mean?: While the NIFTY index has gained 51% over last 365 days, the P/E ratio has significantly moved lower. That implies that market is fairly priced now than it was one year ago. This maybe difficult to believe, but if the numbers are right, that is the fact. And there is no cause to not trust the numbers. We can be wrong: Readers will agree that there is no one with more access to economy data than the RBI governor. With all that data available to him and considering the fact that NIFTY was trading at a very high P/E, he predicted a big correction in the market last year. We all know what has happened since then. RBI governor got it absolutely wrong. Now we see NIFTY much higher and P/E much lower. How could that happen? Because of improvement in earnings. And improvement in earnings is a good sign. Market is poised for greater heights. Only we can not predict it over short term. We may see some correction in the immediate future. Or may not, who knows? Overheated or not: Having stated earlier that the market is not overheated, I would like to add few words of caution here. With markets at all time high, the beaten down stocks suddenly make big up moves. New investors think that the stock is now on road to recovery. In fact, it is nothing of the sort. Soon, these stocks will get back to lower levels. Avoid these stocks. They may look cheap but they do not have value. Some examples are Yes Bank, Idea, India Bulls Housing Finance, Reliance Capital, Reliance Power, PCJ. Suzlon, Jaiprakash Associates and almost all of PSU banks. Question: What happens when a (turbaned) Sikh enters a Hindu Temple? Will the priests not allow them to enter (like Dalits/ untouchables) especially in India?
Answer: What happens when a (turbaned) Sikh enters a Hindu Temple?: Will the priests not allow them to enter ( like Dalits/untouchables ) specially in India?: The question is in two parts. Let us address them one by one. Entering a temple with head covered or bareheaded is different in North and South India. In northern part of the country, it is okay to cover your head. In most temple gatherings, women are generally urged to cover their heads. When the priest is applying Tilak to the forehead of the worshipper, men usually cover the head with their hand. It is normal in North India. Probably it is influenced by the Sikh custom or Muslim practice of covering the head. In South India, nobody covers the head. I have observed this so many times as I lived for many years in the southern states of India. My wife and daughter in law would cover their heads as a matter of habit while no other woman would be doing so. My hand goes instinctively to my head while applying the Tilak but other men do no such thing. Sikh gentlemen and women are regular visitors to Mata Vaishno Devi Temple and other major temples at Haridwar, Varanasi etc. There is no problem with the turban or covered heads. In South India, it is different. There are certain temples where entry is denied to people from other religions. Only Hindus are permitted. Some of them may consider Sikhs as non Hindus. Padmnabhswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, Guruvayoor Temple, Meenakshi Temple in Madurai, Jagannath Temple in Puri do not permit people of other religions. There maybe other such temples too. Many years ago, there was a controversy about the proposed visit of the then President of India, Gyani Zail Singh to Guruvayoor Temple. As per the news of those times, the controversy was about the turban. The priests were not allowing entry with head covered and Giani Zail Singh being a Sikh, could not go without his turban. Mrs. Indira Gandhi was denied entry to Jagannath Puri temple while she was the Prime Minister because she was married to a Parsi and hence considered non Hindu. Some temple signboards: Second part of the question is more of a statement — like Dalits and untouchables are not allowed. As per law there is nobody who is untouchable. As per law, entry of Dalits into temples is not barred. But practices may be different at different places. We may find no discrimination in many places but face extreme prejudice at others. That is a social thing as well as poor implementation of law. Well, these were my thoughts on the subject. No problems in North India. Some issues at few selected temples due to their specific customs. Important Point: Sikh Gurudwaras welcome everyone. Keep your head nicely covered and be blessed by the gurus. Thanks for reading. Question: Which is best Options strategy to consistently earn 0.5% per week (2% pm) with low risk?
Answer: Best options strategy to consistently earn 0.5% per week ( 2% per month ) with low risk?: Let us limit ourselves to earning little more than 2% per month. I would not call it the Best Options Strategy. What I can do, others can do better. It does not matter whether the strategy is best or just about Good. I do not look for returns on weekly basis. A month is a better time frame. Strategy in simple steps: Take the 3 top weight stocks of BANKNIFTY index. Currently these are HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK and AXISBANK. Sell 1 lot of PUTS ( about 2–3% ) away strikes ( Out of money ) in all three stocks. That gives us a credit amount. Buy 3 lots of BANKNIFTY PUTS ( about 4–5% away strikes ) to hedge the previous trades. This will be a debit trade. As a net result we get a credit amount. We call it initial credit. Now we wait. There are 4 possibilities. Stocks move up and perform better than BANKNIFTY —- We get a profit quickly. Stocks move up but do not perform better than the index — Profit comes slowly. Stocks move lower but BANKNIFTY moves much lower —— Again a profit Stocks move lower and do worse than BANKNIFTY —— We get a loss. In case of a quick profit, we exit when we see about 75% of the initial credit as mark to market profit and set up again. The set up costs around Rs. 6.00 lakhs presently including the margins for selling the options and cost of buying the BANKNIFTY PUTS. Results for last 17 months: I have been sharing this strategy on my blog since November 2019. Here are the results: The result is much better than 2% per month. Question: Which stocks should someone buy when Rahul Gandhi becomes PM?
Answer: Which stocks should someone buy when Rahul Gandhi becomes PM?: There are 5 answers to this question. Let us talk from the stock market perspective. Rajiv Gandhi becoming the Prime Minister would be something unexpected. But we have seen people becoming Prime Minister of India unexpectedly. In fact in the 1990s it was a joke that if you want to become the PM, do not contest the Lok Sabha elections. The first person who became Prime Minister unexpectedly was Mr. P V Narasimha Rao. He led a minority government for 5 years. Harshad Mehta scam happened during his tenure. Sensex moved up from 1361 to 3795 in his 5 year tenure. Gain 178%. There was a short lived government of 13 days led by Mr. Atal Bihari Vajpayee after that. Let us forget that. Mr. H. D. Devegowda was the next unexpected Prime Minister. He was followed by yet another dark horse Mr. I.K. Gujral. Both of them held office for little less than 1 year each. Sensex moved from 3886 to 3801 in Devegowda tenure and from 3801 to 3716 in Gujral’s term. Loss 2.1% and 2.2% respectively. After Mr. Gujral it was Mr. Vajpayee again. This time it was an expected outcome. He was in office from 19–03 -1998 to 22–05 -2004 a little more than 6 years. Sensex moved up from 3716 to 5069. Not a big gain but positive returns —- Gain 36.14% In 2004, unexpected happened once again. Dr. Manmohan Singh was the accidental Prime Minister as someone has written a book. But markets were up and up during his tenure and took the crash of 2008 also in its stride. Sensex moved up from 5069 to 24121 in his 10 year tenure. Gain 375% In 2014 and 2019 we saw Mr. Narendra Modi winning the elections. He was expected to win on both occasions and there were no surprises. He is now in office for almost 7 years. Sensex has moved up from 24121 to 49216. Gain 104% ( Numbers are interpolated from the chart — there maybe little inaccuracy but not to make a difference to the conclusions ) Conclusions: Based on these numbers, we can say that market does not care about which party is in power or who is the Prime Minister. It cares for stability of the government and continuity of policies. The maximum gain came during 10 year term of Dr. Manmohan Singh. The five year term of Mr. P V Narasimha Rao also was good with a gain of 175% over that period. Markets are doing fine in the current term of Mr. Modi’s government. Market will survive Mr. Rahul Gandhi too. Market reacts adversely in the beginning. Then it gets back in its stride. It had crashed big when UPA came to power in 2004. And the biggest gains came in UPA tenue. To sum it up, if US markets could survive and flourish with Donald Trump at the helm, Rahul Gandhi is not a threat to Indian stock market. Politics does not impact the market over the long run. Thanks for reading.

Question: As a non Malayali, which was the first Malayalam movie you have seen? Can you share your experience watching it?
Answer: My first Malayalam movie: The year was 1989. I was posted at Lower Periyar Dam Project of Kerala State Electricity Board. My posting at the project was not for a long duration but I enjoyed my brief stay in Kerala. The place of residence was Kothamangalam, a very nice small town. Well, I had become little conversant with Telugu, Tamil and Kannada because of my previous postings and friends in those days. Malayalam was still a mystery. My children began their schooling at Kothamangalam and I became familiar with the alphabets. More of the language came to me through interactions with workers at the construction site. Those were the days of VHS cassettes and VCRs. One could rent a cassette of a movie for a day and watch with a VCP/VCR. I have still got one VCP lying around, most likely non functional as it is unused since the year 2001. That is enough introduction. My boss told that he has rented a cassette for the day and both our families can watch the movie together. He was from Tamil Nadu but could understand Malayalam. For me, it was okay. I had watched Telugu, Tamil and Kannada movies too without knowing the languages. No harm in experimenting again. The movie was: CHEPPU —- A Priyadarshan movie starring Mohanlal in the lead role. The movie was based on the theme of college politics, drugs and violence. Mohanlal played the role of an upright college teacher. I could see the intensity of expressions but the dialogues were beyond me. Helpful explanations from my boss did not help much. Mostly in similar themed movies, hero emerges triumphant in the climax. This movie was different. Hero died. That was poignant and the reason I remember the movie. I understand that it was a big hit too. I did not watch any other Malayalam movie till yesterday. This time it is DRISHYAM 2. Once again it is Mohanlal who carries the film. Cheppu was made in 1987. Mohanlal was the top actor along with Mammootty. Going further, even when something is possible at a particular time, may not be possible at another time. One may succeed in one attempt and fail next time. But the outcome will still be known as POSSIBLE. The Reality: In March 2020, these trades shared on my blog made a profit of nearly Rs. 5.00 lakhs. Let us not live in a world of make believe, a world removed from the reality. We shall see far more failures in trading than we see successes. The key is to keep trying and stay profitable. If the profit in March 2020 gave some ego satisfaction, the rest of the year brought it down many many notches. Here is the result for the full year 2020: The profit for March was higher than the loss in 10 months. I could end the year with some profit. Every trader is different. Results will vary. It is an accepted market wisdom that not more than 10% traders make a profit. Therefore it is safe to assume that 100% in a month kind of profits are possible but not possible to sustain. The aim should be —- Trade cautiously, trade profitably. Big profits are welcome when the market is kind but let us be secure in the knowledge that these occasions will not occur too often. Question: Do professional traders lose money?
Answer: Do professional traders lose money?: Let us first define a professional trader. These are the traders who trade for a living. That could mean that they trade big volumes for themselves or their clients or institutions. Banks and Hedge funds have their trading professionals doing all kind of trades —- Stocks, Currency, Commodities, Interest Rates, Bonds and what not. There are any number of securities to trade and there are many numbers of professional traders. Now coming to their profits and losses. Does year 2008 ring a bell?: The crash of the year 2008 was attributed to sub prime crisis. Housing mortgages which were doubtful in nature were traded many times over by so called professional traders. Everybody dumped the worthless options on each other and when the bubble burst, there was nowhere to hide and no security to hold. Professionals lost money for themselves and their clients. They also caused others not related to these trades also lose money because of the crash. When professionals lose, they do it by truckloads. Only they are saved by the governments. In US it is done by Federal Reserve, in India by the RBI, elsewhere too by the Financial Regulators. These highly paid professionals mess up quite often but their mess is swept under the carpet. Otherwise markets would not look glamorous. One can read this article ( year 2013 ): 5 years after financial crash, many losers — and some big winners You can read about Nick Leeson, a professional trader who caused the fall of a U.K. Bank here: Nick Leeson - Wikipedia Then there was the fall of Lehmann Brothers. Bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers - Wikipedia To Summarize: Every trader loses money at times. Professional or amateur, the distinction does not matter. Professionals come back from the losing situation mostly through their loss management strategy or they are bailed out by the governments. Question: Sensex suffers biggest fall in 10 months. What retail investors should do?
Answer: Sensex biggest fall in 10 months. What should retail investors do?: Retail investors. What can they do or what should they do? In the grand scheme of the stock markets, these people called retail investors do not matter at all. The huge turnover in the market is due to institutional buying and selling. Retail investors just ride piggy back on them. Their logic, thinking and action has no impact on the market. So rather than wondering about what to do, a retail investor should always have an exit plan. There should be a limit placed on the maximum loss to be taken. And there should be no limit on the profit. This is simple to state but difficult to follow. But who said that making money in the stock market was easy? Why worry about the down move now?: We live for instant gratification. And instant panic too. Sensex moves up 1000 point. We are ecstatic even while making no money out of that move. Sensex moves down 1000 points and we start worrying as if it is the end of the world. Let us see what happened over last one month in the market: The index is little higher than where it was a month ago. What is the big deal? What is the worry? Just because someone on business channels becomes paranoid that a big fall is coming should we run for cover? No. We should always have a cover — meaning a stop loss. I am not a bullish person about the market. I generally make my profit when the market goes down. But one fact the retail investors should keep in mind is that the markets are resilient. In last one year we have seen that. Let us have a look at the 1 year chart of the same index. In March 2020, SENSEX had fallen to 25000 levels. Today it is at 49000. Almost double in 1 year. But who could take advantage of this recovery? Those who stayed invested. Those who did not get worried with every decline and not became euphoric with every rise in the index. Let us remember the adage —- It s time in the market that makes money and not timing the market. To Summarize: The best course of action for a retail investor in most situations is —- Do nothing and stay invested. And this time is no different. So same action. To Summarize: Here is something pleasing to the eye: A grassy lawn always looks inviting. But does it look like every time? To get this look, it needs nurturing, weeding and waiting. Good investments are also like that. Grass grows in a week. Investments take longer. Give time to your investments till they get the pleasing look. Other than that, we need to do —- NOTHING. Question: Why is SEBI imposing too many laws, making it difficult for retailers to invest as if markets are for FIIs and DIIs only?
Answer: Why is SEBI making too many laws? As if the markets are for FIIs and DIIs only? SEBI ( Securities & Exchange Board Of India) is the regulator for stock exchanges and money market empowered by the SEBI Act 1992. Well, SEBI does not make laws. That is the job of the government. SEBI makes rules for regulating the market. Like all regulators the heads at SEBI also think that they know best. That is the bane of every regulator and SEBI is no exception. In my view, SEBI has made nothing difficult for INVESTORS. Investors are those people who buy shares in a business for long term. SEBI has made no rules to harm this category. SEBI has done quite a lot to curb speculative trades by TRADERS. Now INVESTORS and TRADERS are two distinct categories. I will talk from the perspective of OPTION TRADERS, that is the market segment with maximum turnover. SEBI rules on OPTION TRADING: Lot Sizes: In early 2015, average lot of a trade was around Rs. 200000. By end of 2015, lot sizes were changed and average trade value became around Rs. 500000. The purpose of the move was to discourage people with insufficient funds to avoid trading in F&O segment. Was SEBI serving a social cause? God only knows. Was it there mandate? Maybe God also does not know. Now we have NIFTY above 15000 and lot size is 75. So trade value of 1 lot of NIFTY is more than Rs. 1125000. In 2015, when NIFTY was around 8200, lot size was 25. Trade value was about Rs. 205000. That has chased away many small traders. Yet option volumes are not going down. That means there is increased participation by the HNIs, FIIs etc. Margins: Sometimes margins are raised to ridiculous levels. Agreed that risk management needs safe margins but there has to be a limit. If you want to sell options or trade in Futures in stocks like Vodafone Idea ( 90% ), IBULHSGFIN ( 100% ) it is just not margin but the entire trade value. Then there are many stocks requiring 40–50% margin. Big lot sizes combined with unreasonable margins make trading in STOCK OPTIONS very difficult. Ostensibly the aim was to prevent speculation but due to higher costs associated with the trades, the stocks become more speculative. One of the primary objectives of stock options is and was —- Portfolio Protection. With these kind of margins, how does one get protection? Too much control has totally spoiled this part of the market. Compulsory Physical Settlement in F&O segment: One of the stupidest regulation by SEBI. SEBI has mandated that F&O contracts will be settled by actual physical delivery of shares. Maybe some great minds had lot of deliberations before making this rule. Fortunately it does not apply to index trades and we still see good volumes in the expiry week. But this rule has killed the trades in STOCK OPTIONS. When this rule was applied to just 42 stocks initially, I had written that it may lead to many stocks being removed from F&O list. That has actually happened. But I had hoped that it will work out better. Probably it would have if OPTIONS BUYERS were not burdened with additional margin on trades doing well ( In The Money Options ) in the expiry week. Even in year 2008, when American Options were traded on NSE, such additional margins were not imposed. That is something SEBI new regulations have done and killed any prospects of small trader benefitting from Option Buying trades. My earlier answer: What's your opinion on SEBI's decision for compulsory delivery instead of cash settlement in derivative options market? Will it discourage retail investors from participating in options market? To Summarize: For better or worse, one has to live with the governments, regulators and rules. What can not be cured must be endured. We suffer in silence ( small traders) while the regulations do not impact those with deep pockets. When did the rich want the poor playing their games? And now they have got the umpire to control the access to the ground. Life is unfair. So be it. We have to keep fighting ( trading ) and winning our small battles irrespective of SEBI. Thanks for reading.

Question: What is the meaning of unlimited profit in options? What are the biggest options profit ever in India?
Answer: Unlimited Profit in Options: It is said that an option ( Call or Put ) has the potential to give an unlimited profit to the buyer of the option. At the same time, it can give unlimited loss to the seller of the option. It is the attraction of the big profit ( unlimited is limited by our own fear and greed ) which brings many people to option buying. But most of them fail to spot these big gains and fail to book the profit even if they are in the trade. Why do we say that sky is the limit? Because that is the limit of our vision. What is the unlimited profit in option buying? It is the amount the market move could give us if we were willing to take it. Biggest Options Profits In India: I have seen quite a few big moves. Some of them were in the trades where I had held that option. I never could book the maximum profit though I have taken a good part of the maximum possible many times. Here are few examples recent and not so recent. December 2020: UPL is a good volatile stock. On December 10, 2020, it tanked more than 15% during the day. That made PUT 400 go from Rs. 0.90 on previous day to Rs. 23.10 on this day. It is another matter that the price of this option is back to Rs. 0.75. Fall of March 2020: We all remember the market crash that came about in March this year. The big fall resulted in many PUT options giving spectacular returns. Here is a snapshot for NIFTY PUT 10000: On March 02, 2020, NIFTY was around 11130 levels. At that time, no one would have thought that the index could go below 10000 level. PUT 10000 was available at a low of Rs. 11.00 during the day. As the market fell and NIFTY kept on moving lower, this is how the PUT price moved. From a low of Rs. 11.00 it moved to a high of Rs. 2451.15 on March 23, 2020. Incredible, but it actually happened. Rs. 825 could become Rs. 183825. This is what is meant by UNLIMITED PROFIT in options. My Trades: I did not take a trade in NIFTY in that month. I bought PUT options in HCLTECH and RBLBANK and the trades were suggested on my blog before the day began. March 2020 - Options Buying - Day 02 HCLTECH PUT 500 was bought for Rs. 6.00 and RBLBANK PUT 260 for Rs. 7.00. This is how these options moved. After buying at Rs. 6.00 , the price moved to Rs. 1.80. Then the fall began and I could exit at Rs. 115.00 on March 19, 2020. A good trade for me in the falling market. In RBL trade, I got out early on March 09, 2020 at Rs. 56.00. I thought that getting 8x value was good enough. Like I stated earlier, we are limited by our fear and greed and that defines UNLIMITED. After my exit, the PUT kept on gaining value and made a high of Rs. 124.85. I left lot of money on the table in this trade. Example with CALL trades: The examples shown above were all for PUT trades. These happened when the markets in general or a particular stock fell sharply. This does not mean that UNLIMITED PROFITS can not come through positive moves. Here is an example of a CALL trade making lot of money. ( Not my trade — just an example ) RELINFRA CALL 500 DEC 2017 Expiry: As the stock price made the big up move, CALL 500 moved from a paltry Rs. 0.60 to Rs. 70.00. That is more than 100 times. I believe that is good enough. To Summarize: Option price moves in a very big manner when the underlying index or stock price makes a good up or down move. It is unlimited in the sense that it is not defined. We consider a big profit as unlimited profit. Such moves keep on happening. They happen far more frequently than what we believe. Only we have to find a way to get into such trades and then to get out also. Not an easy task. But even partial success can give good rewards. The success of my option buying trades ( in spite of recent losses ) mentioned on my blog over last 32 months is a testimony to the above fact —- partial success being rewarding. I hope the answer helped. Thanks for reading.

Question: Are you making the same mistake again and again in trading?
Answer: Are you making the same mistake again and again in trading?: We are human. Humans make mistakes. I would be lying if I say I do not make mistakes. But making the mistakes again and again? A good trader should not do that. I will be lying if I say that I do not make mistakes again and again. Traders who make repeated mistakes are not good traders. Every mistake in the market costs money. It causes losses. Those making repeated mistakes can not remain profitable. Repeating the mistakes makes me a bad trader and probably a losing trader. The answer is complete: I have answered what was asked. But I am not known for short answers. Secondly, what good can come out of knowing the fact that I make same mistake again and again. So here is the long answer: I write a blog about options trading. The main theme there is Option Buying. Almost everyone says that buying options can never be profitable. It was a challenge to prove this statement wrong. And to prove it wrong over a period of time. Recently I got a comment about my way of trading. “foolishness is a person doing the same thing again and again and expecting different results, same here, thank God, there was covid, else I just wonder what would have been the case “ It is implied that my way of trading was a mistake and I am doing the same thing again and again. I have said it earlier and somebody else too said it for me. Well, different strokes for different folks. What works for me may not work for others. Trades may go the same way but it is how much you make from a good trade that makes the difference. My response to the above comment was: “Surely I am foolish when I make losses. I always accept that fact. But I am just lucky when I get a big profit. I am not expecting different results. I expect same results. The results that came in the year 2018 and 2019. If you take out the blinker of a colored vision where you refuse to see the truth, the year 2020 is still profitable even after booking a loss of Rs. 28500 for another bad month in September. A big part of profit has vanished but still it is a profit of Rs. 130000 for the year 2020. And believe me there was no COVID in 2018 and 2019 when those profits came through.” Let us talk about the repeated mistakes. I often make the mistake of being wrong in the trade. But do not make the mistake of exiting with a profit lower than what the market wants to give me. At times it is frustrating as the profit just vanishes while I wait for a bigger profit. At those times I think I am being foolish, stupid and whatever else comes to mind. But when I sit back and analyze, I find it was those big profits ( which came through waiting ) that have kept me in the game for so long. I might have written the profit for the year till September 2020 as about Rs. 130000. It is actually better than that till end of November 2020 at Rs. 165072. And for the 31 month period since I started writing about option buying, the profit is —- Rs. 875920. It is another matter that profit at the end of March was Rs. 1245213. What no one bothers to note is that the loss over 8 losing months ( April - November 2020 ) is less than the profit of 1 month of March 2020. That is the most essential aspect of my trading which is lost to everyone else but always remains at the back of my mind. I follow the Jesse Livermore dictum: An option buyer knows that his loss can not go beyond a limit which is already known. I go for the second part of this saying —- Hope that the profit becomes bigger. This is the mistake I make repeatedly. Probably I will keep on doing that. Thanks for reading.

Question: How do you come to realize that the stock market is often wrong?
Answer: How do you come to realize that stock market is often wrong?: Interesting question. The assumption in the question is that the stock market is often wrong. In February of this year, coronavirus was a murmur. It became a full blown news item in March with many people dying all over the world. Lock downs were imposed and many businesses came to a standstill. Markets crashed everywhere. Market was right in going down. The future looked bleak at that point of time and market is always about the future. My trades were on the down side and I made good money in those two months. Market was right and I was right. Coronavirus has not gone away. People are still dying from it. UK and Germany are looking at imposing lock down again. Vaccine is still to be found and be available. Some businesses have recovered, others are limping along. Market has put the past behind and moved ahead determinedly. Like I said earlier, it is all about future. NIFTY chart for the tear 2020 tells the story. It is higher than where it was in January. I kept thinking that markets will move lower as businesses have been seriously impacted. Profitability is low, banks face more defaults and inflation will rise. Hence market should take these factors into account and move lower. Coronavirus caused havoc, number of cases kept increasing and so did number of deaths. Market should certainly move lower. That was my thinking. I kept trading that way. The results were not flattering. April, May, June 2020: In 3 months, I suffered a loss of Rs. 167509. July to October 2020: I thought market is not right. It can not stay this way forever. I kept trading in the same manner. Mostly I banked on stocks moving lower with an occasional trade in the positive direction. The summary of results: All losses. July —- Rs. 63297 Aug — Rs. 33310 Sep — Rs. 28500 Oct —- Rs. 32580 Loss in these 4 months —- Rs. 157687 Combined loss in 7 months —- April to October 2020 —- Rs. 325196. I am supposed to be a good trader. Lots of people follow me here on Quora. I teach people how to trade options. I write a blog on option trading. And these are very unflattering results over a 7 month period. Why? Because I thought market was wrong. The fact is market is never wrong. We traders are wrong. You and me can be wrong but not the market. It is just loss management that I am still keeping my head above water for the year because of the big profit in March 2020. That is the way to trade. When the market gives you a profit, try to cash it big. At other times, try to keep the losses within limit. To Summarize: I never came to realize that markets are wrong. The results of last 7 months very clearly tell me that market is always right. I am wrong. There is no point in arguing with what the market does. Argument does not make money. Trading with the trend does. Remember the very old market wisdom: Market is always right. Thanks for reading. Images : Google Images and OptionsNext.com

Question: What is the best way to earn money in the stock market?
Answer: Best way to earn money in the stock market?: Back to basics. I have answered more than 500 questions on stock market related topics but this gem eluded me so far. Different tools of trading: I could talk about margin trading, futures trading, options buying, options strategies, forex trading, commodity futures and options or plain simple long term investment in good stocks and mutual funds. We have to keep them small. Exit the loss making trades with a small loss and stay with the profitable trades to maximize the gain. Question: Have you ever met a celebrity in your life?
Answer: Today I take a break from my stock market writings and select a simple topic to write about. I am nearing 64 years of age now. Meeting a celebrity ( meaning a famous person ) to me means having a little more than a handshake. Nowadays it is about taking a selfie with them. Our times were different. In my college days I had the opportunity to have small interactions with Ch. Bansi Lal , Sr. Swaran Singh and Sh. Jagjivan Ram. Photos were taken by a photographer but that was in 1973, 1972 and 1971 and today those black and white images are not available. Later during my working career , I had the opportunity to meet the following ministers in Rajiv Gandhi, V P Singh and P V Narasimha Rao Governments —- Sushila Rohatgi, Kalp Nath Rai and V C Shukla. Today’s generation may not know them but they were important politicians of those days. We live in the times of selfies and instant videos. I have two of them to share here: Here I am with Mr. Chetan Sharma, former India Cricketer. He is best known for his hat trick in one day cricket and for the last ball six hit by Javed Miandad in a match at Sharjah which cost India that match. This photo is from the year 2014. We talked about both the above events and his forays into politics. The meeting lasted about 30 minutes and just when he was leaving, I thought of getting a photo. Another one: I believe this needs no introduction. It brings back poignant memories as Mrs. Sushma Swaraj is no longer among us. The affable and well liked former External Affairs Minister left for her heavenly abode on August 06, 2019. This photo is from year 2012 when she was the leader of opposition, Lok Sabha. We had this interaction for about 40 minutes where we talked about the state of affairs in politics, how the elections will work out in 2014 ( Mr. Modi was not in national picture at that time ) and about the past. Both of us studied in the same college but not in the same years. My father taught in that college and she was his favorite student. That is how this meeting came about easily. Today, only the memories remain. Another celebrity meeting ( a long one ) which I would like to forget was with Prof. Ravindra Gaekwad, in the year 2017 when he was a Member of Parliament from Osmanabad in Maharashtra. He is the gentleman who beat an Air India staffer with a chappal. Luckily for me, I could get out of the meeting with some harsh words only. Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words would never hurt me. Such sayings must be meant for these kind of celebrity encounters. Well, these were my few brushes with the famous people. Question: What is something no one will tell you about investing in blue chip stocks?

Question: Why do people show only their profit and not loss in the stock market?

A trader is a god trader if he/she made money from the trades based on a method and generally sticking to that method. It does not matter that there were a number of losing trades in between before the profit was seen. There are about 10% of the traders who are profitable. Other 90% too get profit from time to time but the final outcome is a loss. The successful 10% too have losses but are able to manage that the losses stay less than the profit earned. It is mostly by loss management that a trader is successful. Why they do not show their losses?: Because it makes them look bad. Because it hurts the ego. Question: Is it true that 43% of the train fare is borne by the common citizens of the country?
Answer: On a lazy Sunday, I take a break from my stock market answers and come back to my hobby of the 1980s —- Indian Railways. There is lot of talk about 43% of fares being subsidized. Well, here is my take on the subject. Indian Railways are struggling with the the problems of a huge work force, monumental inefficiency, political interference , old rolling stock and so much more. All these factors lead to annual losses. There is a limit to which the ticket price can be increased. Rather than correcting themselves, Railways with come up with a half truth —- 43% of the train fare is borne by the common citizens of this country. What is so special about it? You and me are that common citizen. We have been paying for the inefficiency of the government since ages. I paid my first income tax in 1981. Still paying at at 64. No regrets. But why the government should keep telling me that 43% of the fare is subsidized? I have been contributing to this subsidy all my life by paying my taxes. And it is not for a noble cause like helping the poor. It is in the stupid cause of supporting the inefficiency of the Indian Railways or most of other government departments. Governments are the past masters in telling and propagating lies and this lie about 43% of train fares being subsidized is another deceit foisted on the gullible. It is the mindset: Indian Railway does not run like a commercial enterprise or like a service provider. It runs with a colonial mindset. Their are rules, rules, exceptions and fines of so many types that few books could be written about them. With all those rules, regulations, efforts to fine people ( customers actually ) and all the other related nonsense, Railways fail to make money. Who is to be blamed? Not the Chairman of Railway Board, not the Railway Minister. It is your fault and mine. We are availing too many concessions and enjoying low fares.Every minister keeps repeating the lies. A lie repeated many times starts looking like truth. And we the people, poor suckers are trapped within those lies. By the which service provider imposes fines on its customers? Yes, other than Railways, State Electricity Boards , Road Transport Corporations come to mind. Same story there too. Inefficient service and treating the customer as some sort of criminal. These enterprises suffer from the same mindset. Let us see through the lies: This is what the 2 AC ticket New Delhi to Bangalore costs for a journey on December 05, 2020 ( 2 months away ): Rs. 3655 is the fare. Journey duration is 33 hrs 25 minutes. And while buying the ticket I will be reminded that 43% of the fare is being subsidized. Insulting the customer while being inefficient in doing your own job. Now let us look at other alternative and other service providers i.e . Airlines. This is what a flight ticket would cost me: Rs. 3388 for a 2 hour 40 minute flight on the same date. The fare is almost same in other airlines too. The journey takes less time and I do not get insulted by the service provider. What would be my choice? I think it is obvious. To Summarize: Governments are in the habit of telling lies. It does not matter which party is in power. Telling lies is an ingrained quality of the politicians and those in government in any capacity. I have been in public sector and have collaborated with the government authorities in fabricating many lies ( in highway sector ), I know what I am saying. Let us not believe what the Railways tell us. We are the customers. We should demand and expect quality service for the money we pay. What we get instead is shoddy service, lot of platitudes and disguised insult by telling us that the fare is subsidized. Public can be fooled all the time is the belief with which governments function and at most time their belief is true. Fault lies with us. As far as Railways is concerned, we should vote with our feet —- by avoiding the train travel. Simple response —- you are telling us that tickets are subsidized. I accept the fact and I do not want to put the burden on our great Indian Railways. I will not use your services. Thank you very much. If all of us do that where does that leave those talking about subsidy? I know it is not likely to happen. We have got accustomed to the lies peddled by the government that our independent thinking has taken a back seat. Well, take this answer as the rants of an old man. But it is not a lie. Thanks for reading.

Question: What happens when a stock market crashes?
Answer: What happens when stock market crashes?: Here are few things I observed during the market crashes in the year 2001, 2008 and most recently in March 2020. (1) The decibel level of the anchors and experts on business channels goes up. They keep giving a positive spin to the worst of news also and keep telling that it is a buying opportunity. That proves true in few cases but is absolutely wrong in many stocks. But this always happens. (2) Everyone and their uncle will ask you about the market even though these people would not have invested a single rupee in the market. (3) Some people like me, who had short positions during the crash will make good money and then talk about it for years on Quora or their blogs. I do it all the time. (4) Many fortunes are lost. Those people blame the market and vow never to come back again. Half of them actually do that, other half come back to the market with reduced capital and keep trying their luck. (5) Banking and automobile companies stocks are generally the worst hit in the crash. The exception was 2001, when it was called the dot com bubble. (6) The regulators all over the world try to bolster the market by throwing more money in the market. This throwing of money is given a glorious name like —- stimulus package. (7) Some people will try to average their buying. Unless they have really strong risk appetite , these people will be the ones to suffer maximum losses. There can be few exceptions but I do not see people averaging in RELIANCE but keep doing that in RCOM or SUZLON. We know what happens in such cases. (8) At some point, the down move will come to a halt. Some stocks would have fallen to the extent that they are beyond recognition. Such stocks will be moved out of the index. NIFTY will be revised and based on the recovery in few top stocks it will move up. Nobody will talk about the stocks which were taken out of index but real investors would be sitting with them nursing their wounds. Some will keep wondering for entire lifetime why their investments are not making money even while markets were making new highs. (9) Finally markets will come back to previous level. I will keep wondering when the next crash is coming and miss all the gains that could have come from the recovery. Some people will get lucky during this recovery phase and claim to be great at assessing the market. I will wait for my chances as and when the next crash comes around. No one will get wiser. I know it because I have seen in happening so many times. Bulls and bears keep fighting. No one wins. (10) Very few traders/investors will learn about hedging, risk management and strategies during the crash. These are the people who will not be impacted during the next crash. Number of such participants is generally around 1–2%. Most notable thing that happens when the market crashes: Your mutual funds investments will bleed. They will show negative results even when the market recovers. But all the time the fund managers will keep posing as if they are the God’s gift to the market and the investors. You will not hear a word of apology from them for ruining your investments. We all could ruin our investments in the same manner ourselves without the management expenses. In every stock market crash, mutual funds managers keep their bull shitting at the maximum level. This was my take on what happens when the stock market crashes. Now those who were taken out of index at various points of time in these 5 years. BHEL: VODAFONE IDEA: IBULLHSGFIN: I think these 3 examples are enough to make the point that some stocks ( and some investors ) never come back into profitability even when the market recovers. To Summarize: Boom and bust are the nature of the market. One has to live with them. Talking about the crash never made money for anyone nor did talking about the market highs. Question: Is the stock market a zero-sum game?
Answer: I do not understand the fascination for such questions. I also do not understand what benefit will be derived by knowing the answer. How is it going to change someone’s life if it was a zero sum game or of it was not. Let us see what is a zero sum game. What is meant by zero sum game? Zero-sum is a situation in game theory in which one person's gain is equivalent to another's loss, so the net change in wealth or benefit is zero. A zero-sum game may have as few as two players or as many as millions of participants. Source : Wikipedia Stock markets are trading platforms where millions of traders/investors participate. Many lose the money and few of them make money. Money of the losers goes to the money of gainers. But is it really like a game? The answer would be —- NO. Let us say A buys a stock at Rs. 100 today. It was sold to A by B who had bought it two years ago at Rs. 70. B’s gain is not A’s loss. Because of the good performance of the company the stock price had moved up over last two years and A now expects it do better in the coming years. Five years later, A sells it for Rs. 300. Let us say the buyer is C. One year after C had bought the stock, he needs money for something else and the stock price is down to Rs. 270. He sells it for a loss of Rs. 30. B had a gain of Rs. 30. A had a gain of Rs. 200. C had a loss of Rs. 30. Is it a zero sum situation? Not at all. Why such questions?: Those who want to make money, they take the plunge and invest or trade. Some succeed and some do not. Those who are afraid to act, they keep asking such questions. No action. no success. But success was not the goal here. The goal was just to keep oneself busy with esoteric questions while doing nothing. Life is like that. We are born, we die. Is that a zero sum game? Why do we live, work and do all the things to make it a good life? Because life exists between the two points of birth and death. Why do we trade? Because there exist multiple opportunities to make money. It is like any other venture. The success rate is similar to the success rate in any other profession or business. We see successful lawyers, we see struggling lawyers. We see successful players, we see players struggling with issues of form and injury. We see Mukesh Ambani, we see Anil Ambani. Shall we act or just sit on the fence pontificating about the life being a zero sum game or stock market being a zero sum game. First of all, stock market is not a game. Those who would approach it as a game to enjoy, will neither get the enjoyment nor the money. If it all it is a game, zero sum or not, one has to approach it with the attitude of a winner and succeed. To Summarize: In many of my earlier answers I have written that stock markets are the microcosm of life. Market ups and downs are like the good times and bad times in a persons life. We work hard in bad times, we try to learn more, earn more, compromise more in order to find solutions to the problems life throws at us. Same way we need to work hard, learn from failures and gain knowledge to overcome the difficult situations and become successful. Talking about life and stock markets being zero sum games is of no use. Life is there to be lived. Markets are there for investment and trading. Thanks for reading.

Question: Is it pointless to expect logic in market moves?
Answer: Is it pointless to expect logic in market moves?: On a day to day basis, it is pointless to expect logic. Market generally over reacts to almost every news, good or bad. We have seen many examples of that. Three years ago, it was North Korea related news that used to spook the market. Still logic works: It is said that the market is a voting machine in the short term but over long term it is a weighing machine. Over time, cream floats to the top i.e. good stocks out perform the rest of market. A good portfolio of stocks out performs the index at most of time. Logically, it should be always but in reality it is most of time. The reason is what we discussed earlier. Market can be irrational due to fear and greed. Market moves are driven by money. Stock price goes up if there are people buying it for right reasons or wrong and it goes down when people are willing to sell it for just the same reasons. Both buyers and sellers have a reason. Both have a logic. One logic works, other logic fails. If we are on the wrong side of the trade, we feel that logic does not work in the market. If we are right, we pat ourselves on the back and consider that we know everything about the market. It is not too much to expect logic to work. It is too much to expect our logic to work every time. No individual is bigger than the market. It would pay to go with the flow. For every price, there is a buyer and seller. Somebody’s logic is working. Profit in market is not derived from the number of successful trades. It is derived from how much profit you make from the successful trades. To summarize: Like elsewhere in life, we need to approach the market too logically. Only not expect the logic to work every time. There is something called flawed logic and at times we may be guilty of it. Market is always right. Make that your touchstone. Thanks for reading.

Question: How will reducing the repo rate by 40 basis points from 4.4% to 4%, by RBI governor Shaktikanta Das, help reviving the Indian economy?
Answer: How will reducing the repo rate by 40 basis point from 4.4% by RBI, help revive the Indian economy? : The question is —- How? It assumes that this action will have some role in the likely revival. Wrong assumption. Cutting the repo rates is not something new. It has been done so many times in the past, every time with same platitudes attached to it. We are living in strange times where those in charge of policy have distanced themselves from plain common sense. They attach so much importance to their petty actions and decisions. Every decision is meant to bring a significant change in our life. It surely does. Mostly it makes things worse. Did demonetization achieve anything other than just change in the look of currency notes? Did linking of Aadhar Card with your bank account provide you with world class banking? Same thing with RBI rate cuts. They happen quite regularly. It is like a doctor prescribing a larger dose of medicine for an ailing patient in the hope that it will be a cure. But the patient is not responding. Nothing is different this time. Have a look at the repo rates for the past. In last one year, repo rate has come down from 5.75% to 4.00%. Bringing it down from 5.75 % to 4.4 % did not boost the economy. Why additional 0.4% cut will do that? On every occasion in the past, these rate cuts were hailed as a great break through which are going to put the economy back on track. Every time the anchors on business channels were ecstatic as if a miracle cure has been found. A horse can not run faster than its inherent ability. There is a popular horse racing saying. “Putting more weight may slow down a horse, but reducing the weight will not make it run faster than its inherent ability.” Indian economy is that horse with reduced ability due to multiple reasons. Interest rate was the weight. That is being reduced but it still keeps moving on its own slow pace. There is no acceleration, no sign of a quick spurt to victory. You can not make it run faster than its poor ability. Only way it can be done is by cheating the clock. We have done in the past by changing the way GDP was calculated. But economy and industrial production are realities. They do not get revived just by changing the numbers. What after this? : Who cares? Who told us that governments care for economy? They are here for getting voted back to power. Good economy was never good for politics of winning elections. We shall see more rate cuts and if at all there is an improvement in economy, that will not be due to these repo rates. That would be due to enhanced demand when people have more money to spend. Till that time, let us keep on having the same discussion every time RBI reduces the rates. A futile pursuit. Thanks for reading. Image : Global -Rates.com
