The twists in the romantic tale are too many to distract from the struggle theme. For whatever reasons, I liked the K. Balchander movie better. Capturing the psyche of unemployed youth of 1980s : Movies are a social medium. They reflect the times, at times capturing the mood of the society perfectly. There was Do Bigha Zamin ( 1953 ) , Mother India ( 1957 ), Jis Desh Mein Ganga Behti Hai ( 1960 ) , Mere Apne ( 1971 ) , Do Boond Paani ( 1971) Roti Kapda Aur Makaan ( 1974 ) which expressed the feeling of angst and helplessness in the prevailing situations of those times. I understand that there were many more outstanding films but I might have missed them like Pyaasa and Kagaz Ke Phhol. Please excuse my diversion to Hindi movies because I have not seen too many Tamil movies. Both these movies while good to watch did not capture the mood of youth of that time. I can tell that with certainty because I was young and new in a job at that time. Youth of that time were full of hope. They had just seen a government voted out of power and then voted back again. They had dreams and were willing to work towards those dreams. The poverty was real and stark. But the poor did not wear it like a badge. The young among them were trying to break out of poverty through education and finding whatever work was available. They knew that corruption existed but they also knew that life without corruption is also feasible. Both these movies did not capture that spirit. These movies were meant to cash the pathos. The protagonists were portrayed as victims, not the heroes with a vision. To Sum Up : These movies did not capture the spirit of the youth of that time. Still, these were good movies, with good scripts and great performances. I enjoyed them some 40 years ago. To remember so many years later is a testimony to their place in cinema. Question: Whether the sell in May and go away strategy for equity markets will hold good for May 2020 also, amidst already massive fall in global equity indices?
Answer: Sell in May and go away. Will it hold good for May 2020 also? The question implies that this strategy or saying actually worked in earlier years too. That premise is false. That assumption is wrong. The tussle between the bullish and bearish sentiment is always present in the market. Month of the year does not matter. At some point of time in the past, few May months might have shown a negative trend. That is how a catchy slogan is born. That is what it is and nothing more. That is not how one makes profit in the market and that is also not how losses are avoided. It is always prudent to check the facts. In Indian Stock Market, NIFTY is the index which represents the state of the market. I have checked the data for the month of May for 10 years — from 2010 to 2019. Compared NIFTY closing price on the first trading day of the month ( that is when you sell and go away ) with the closing price on the last day of the month. NIFTY closed negative for the month in the first 4 years from 2010 to 2013. From 2014 to 2019 ( 6 years ) , it is positive for the month. So there is no truth in the saying. Market moves are always random. We try to read too much into them unnecessarily. These kind of exercises never helped anybody make money in the market. Will it hold good this time? : For all we know, NIFTY may end up in the red for the month. It has not done that for last 6 times. So there is a likelihood just based on law of averages. So what? Nifty going up or down does not make money. Good trades and investments do. Let us keep our focus there and not lose our way chasing half baked and much hyped sayings which do not mean anything. Question: How would you explain the future and options to a 5-year-old kid?

So here is my answer: I will try this. First of all I will give him/her this definition to study and tell me whether anything could be understood. “What Is Implied Volatility – IV? Implied volatility is a metric that captures the market's view of the likelihood of changes in a given security's price. Investors can use it to project future moves and supply and demand, and often employ it to price options contracts. Implied volatility is not the same as historical volatility, also known as realized volatility or statistical volatility. The historical volatility figure will measure past market changes and their actual results.” Source : Investopedia Hopefully, the child will run away. Let us say the child is persistent. I will throw the Black Scholes Option Pricing formula at him/her as my next point: Surely no 5 year old will want to learn after this. Then I will ask the child to bring the parents and tell them not to put so much burden on the child. There is a time and place for everything. Trading of any kind, leave alone Futures and Options is not meant for 5 year olds. Let the children enjoy their days of innocence. Life awaits them for teaching all other lessons. I will not explain Futures and Options to a 5 year old. Thanks for reading.

Question: What do you think about the extension of lockdown by another two weeks up to May 17? Do you think it will be of help and economically viable?
Answer: Thanks for A2A Nagarajan sir. What do I think about extension of lock down till May 17?: Choice is between the devil and deep see. Choice is about dying from the virus or dying from hunger. Virus is present right now, hunger is waiting around the corner. Choice is not to be made by me. We have given that right to those whom we elected to run the governments. Choice made by the government may work out or may not work out because they are as clueless as you and me. Only they can not admit it. They are under constant scrutiny in these times of acute crisis and they have to be seen to be doing something. But what do you do when really there is no solution. You try many things by doing the minimum work required. The easy way was to extend the lock down. Government took that option. Will it help? : Probably. It will probably help in controlling the spread of the virus. On the other hand, the act of opening up certain activities may put paid to that hope. Suddenly we find trains running full of passengers going back to their villages. Even if a few stray cases carry the virus from the big urban cities to the villages of hinterland, we have a full blown crisis on our hands. Punjab is already seeing that effect with many pilgrims who returned from Huzoor Saheb, Nanded ( Maharashtra) were found positive. All that quarantine and isolation arrangements are putting additional pressure on the health and police personnel who are already working under tremendous strain. Extending the lock down and relaxing the norms is counter productive. But like I said earlier, it is not a choice that can be made easily. Will it be economically viable?: Absolutely not. Let us assume that lock down is lifted on May 17, 2020. We shall be happy that a burden has been lifted. That is all. Shall we go on outings as we used to do in the not so recent past? Shall we go to shopping malls and cinema? Will spectator sport events like cricket matches resume? Will anyone board a train to travel somewhere unless absolutely necessary? The corona virus has cast a sinister shadow on our lives and it will not go away soon. Even before the pandemic, we were talking about recession. Now it will be depression. No doubt that at some stage we shall come out of it. Human will finally triumphs over all adversities and it will do this time too. But the process will be long and painful. We have to bear with the pain. What we can do? : It is clear that our views do not matter at all in the bigger scheme of things. And the views of the high and mighty too do not matter in the God’s scheme of things. Whatever action we take will always be debatable because there are no yes/no type of solutions. Those of us who are fortunate enough that we do not worry about our daily earnings and loss of livelihood, can take care of one poor family for the duration of crisis. It will not be a big strain on our resources and a big help for those who need the help. We do not know how the government help is reaching the needy people but we shall be ensuring that at least a family of 3–5 persons is managing to eat and survive. The pandemic gives lot of power to the government to interfere in our choices and way of living. Not the right way a democracy should function. For a while, we can live with it but let us not lower the guard. Governments do not want to give up the control once they get it. That would be our social responsibility after the crisis is over. Till then, let us follow the guidelines. Let us get inspiration from this saying of Swami Vivekanand: Human will shall prevail. Thanks for reading.

Question: Why was Republic TV head Arnab Goswami questioned by Mumbai Police for more than 10 hours in relation to his comments on Sonia Gandhi?
Answer: Why was Arnab Goswami questioned by Mumbai Police for more than 10 hours in relation to his comments on Sonia Gandhi?: Simple Answer : There are multiple FIRs filed against Arnab Goswami. Once an FIR is filed, police has to investigate the case and find out whether the charges made out in the FIR have any merit. Questioning is part of the investigation process. If the investigation reveals that prima facie no case exists, the FIR will be closed. Otherwise it will go to court and the process of determining the guilt starts. It is just a process. We should not be concerned about it. Few other points: Arnab has very vociferously maintained that one should prove his innocence in the court of law. One should go through the process without a worry. He said so in case of P. Chidambaram , A. Raja , Shashi Tharoor and many others of the same ilk. Now that the shoe is on your own foot, it is hurting. Is it something new that we are getting worked up?: Arnab Goswami is a big celebrity. That does not make him immune from the process of law. He said something. He had every right to say it. Some people have the view that what he said amounts to hate speech. They filed the FIRs. Inquiry and if required a court will determine whether it was a crime. You and me have no role in that. Charges made out in the FIRs may be absolute bull shit but once filed, investigation has to be done. It happens to everyone?: Arnab is a grown up person with great connections. He runs a TV news channel. He spouts questions and answers with lot of sarcasm on the panelists on his show and most of the time gets away because that is a controlled environment. Real life is not a controlled environment. Questioning by Police will not happen in the TV studio. It will not end at the time scheduled for discussion. The tone and tenor of the question will be decided bu someone other than you. That is life. Just two months ago, 9 year old school children were questioned by police in Bidar, Karnataka. Where was the hue and cry? Bidar school sedition case: More students questioned Bidar sedition case: Karnataka child rights body says police violated norms by questioning children In that case too, some parties filed a case against the school and Karnataka Police went into overdrive. Today we are blaming Uddhav Thackerey government, then it was BJP government led by Yeddiyurappa. No political party is above reproach All behave similarly. We may find some perverse pleasure by putting the blame on Sonia Gandhi and say that she is vindictive. But that is just a lame and convenient argument. Arnab used to taunt and mock the Manmohan Singh government on a daily basis when UPA was the ruling dispensation. No action of any type was initiated by Congress party in those days against his utterances. Do we really think that Congress has suddenly become more powerful now when actually it has been rejected by the people? Arnab is a journalist. These type of incidents come with the territory. You ruffle some feathers, someone will rough you up, literally or metaphorically. Ask it from the journalists in Uttar Pradesh : Three journalists held for ‘defamatory’ content on Yogi Journalist booked for comment against Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath This case is just 3 weeks old. Why the hue and cry over Arnab episode and not about these journalists? To Summarize: News on TV is just entertainment that too of the vile variety. The people are peddling their opinions and not the news. We are the gullible consumers who are making heroes out of men of straw. Arnab too is a normal Indian citizen who has a tendencies to go over the top. This time some people decided to call his bluff. So he has to go through the ordeal. Finally nothing will come out of it. None of us will be wiser for it. Soon we shall be talking about some similar nonsense. The fault does not lie with Sonia Gandhi or Maharashtra Government. The fault does not lie with Yogi Adityanath or Yeddiyurappa Governments for the cases mentioned in this answer. The fault lies with you, me and all of us. We do not care for freedom of speech of others. The day comes when my freedom of speech is under threat. That is when it hurts and we cry and nobody listens. Authorities become authoritarian and they know nobody will care for your rights because you were uncaring when other’s rights were being denied. We are busy scoring minor points and forgetting that it is not the celebrities whose voice is being silenced. We are giving away our right to free speech by being selective. Well, for once Arnab Goswami is answering questions instead of asking them. A good change though we know it is all a sham and nothing will come out of it. Thanks for reading. .

Question: Is it a good time to invest in bank stocks for the long term?
Answer: Is it a good time to invest in Bank Stocks for the long term ? : Banks are meant to be a profitable and good business. The business is simple. Get money from people at a cost. Lend it to other people at higher rate of interest than the bank pays on deposits. The difference should be enough to take care of the expenses ( salaries and establishment expenses ) and deliver a net profit. But in modern times, simple things get complicated. Governments start interfering with the banks’ working. Banks are made to give loans that are not viable and to the borrowers without good credentials. In India, we had Loan Melas in the time of Rajiv Gandhi’s government which was a brainchild of Janardhan Poojai, MOS Finance. Presently we have MUDRA loans. These type of loans along with the frauds like Nirav Modi or bad loans like Kingfisher Airlines, Jet Airways, Air India, Reliance Communication, Vodafone Idea, Bhushan Steel and many more sit heavily on the banks’ balance sheets. In the present state of affairs Bank Stocks in India are not a good long term investment. My answer is more specific to public sector banks. This a screen shot from my trades in February 2015: The two bank stock trades are highlighted. Five years ago, CANARA BANK was trading at a price of more than Rs. 440. On Friday, April 17,2020, the closing price is Rs. 86.85. The biggest public sector bank, State Bank of India shares were trading at a price higher than Rs. 300 five years ago. On Friday, April 17 the stock price went up considerably after the press briefing of RBI Governor and was quoted at Rs. 193.25. And five years is a considerably long period of time. The trend remains the same: If one keeps on doing same thing and expects different results, it would be foolishness. But our banks keep doing the same all the time. It is the chatter of the cheer leaders on the business channels who build the hype which makes the stock prices go up from time to time. People start believing that these stocks are good. Government rushes in and gives a dose of liquidity by way of recapitalization and more people buy these stocks to send the prices higher. That is when the smart money makes the exit and the general public is left holding the duds. A big injection of public funds was given to public sector banks in October 2017. Immediately the stock prices shot up. The gains were 25–50% in a single day as if all the problems of the sector were resolved. Then in August 2019, more money was given to these banks and 10 banks merged into 4. Let us look at the prices from October 2017 to present. I have not updated for April 17, 2020 but that is not going to be much different. Every one of these stocks have lost value in this period in spite of government putting in good money in these banks. Private Sector : We do not know who is hiding what. If there are few good performers like HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, AXISBANK and KOTAKBANK, we have YESBANK, RBLBANK and INDUSINDBANK which have performed extremely bad. The sector is troubled already. Troubles will not go away just by RBI relaxing the lending norms. In fact that will lead to more trouble in the future. To Conclude : Banking in present times is not the old sedate method of making money for the business and the stock holders. It is now a high risk business full of dubious decisions, encouraged by the governments and the regulators to take more risks in the name of ease of doing business. Others are enjoying that easing whereas banks bear the brunt of bad loans and defaults. The cycle will never stop because the banks are not being run as banks but money giving institutions without expectations of getting it back. This is a harsh conclusion but unfortunately true. Neither the banks or the government will accept this harsh truth but truth has a way of finally prevailing and it shows itself in the stock prices after some time. Banking stocks are not a good investment. These are my thoughts and views. Readers are welcome to differ. Thanks for reading.

Question: Is it a good time to invest in stocks of PSU banks in India? BOB, SBI or any other stocks you can recommend. Investment horizon is for long term.
Answer: Is it a good time to invest in stocks of PSU banks in India? : This question was posted here sometime in the year 2016. We are now in April 2020. Markets have seen multiple all time highs and given up significantly over last 3 months due to COVID -19 spread throughout the world. Let us revisit the question in the present time. On October 24, 2017 , then then Finance Minister Arun Jaitley made a televised announcement about recapitalization of Public Sector Banks. Announcement came just 10 minutes before the market close. There was some positive move immediately but the big move was to come next day. Most of the PSU Bank stocks went up 30-60% next day. A great day for these stocks. People were lapping up the stocks as if they found the key to Midas Gold. What happened next?: Stock market is a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term. It weighed, separated the grain from the chaff and told us that mostly it was chaff only. There was more recapitalization, relaxation of norms by the RBI and another set of mergers announced by the present Finance Minister in August 2019. Merging three bad banks does not make one good bank. But market players never learn. They rush in to buy these duds whereas the real smart people take this opportunity to sell the worthless stock to all who are willing to buy. Let us have a look at how these stocks went up in a day in October 2017 and where they sit currently. NIFTY has declined 11.5% in this period. Among these PSU Banks, SBI is the stock with minimum loss which is 42.21%. There are 6 stocks which have lost more than 80% of the value. Who needs Nirav Modi and who needs a fraud to get money from these banks? Just go short on these stocks and make money. Unfortunately, many of them are not in F&O segment. In that case, do not invest in them and save money. Conclusion : Throwing good money after bad does not work even if the money belongs to Government. A bad business remains a bad business unless the business practices change. There maybe some rebound at some stage but these stocks remain on the AVOID list. Question: If the coronavirus lock-down is extended till the 30th of April 2020 in India, what would the poor people do?
Answer: If the coronavirus lock down is extended till the 30th of April 2020 in India, what would the poor people do? : The deadly virus has infected more than a million people worldwide now. Those who are not infected are also affected. The effects are different for different set of people but not good for any of them. Let us see what they would do if the lockdown is extended. Government Efforts : There is tendency among the affluent and the well to do class to put the blame on the Government for everything that goes wrong. The same class also sings praise of the tokenism like clapping or lighting lamps to bolster the mood of the nation. The fact is that these are desperate times. Only the poor people are able to cope up better because they face desperation almost on a daily basis even without the threat of a lock down. Earlier at least they could move out in search of work to earn their daily wages. If they could find work it was alright, otherwise it was desperation. Now it is desperation every moment as even the hope of finding work is taken away by the lockdown. I will talk of Haryana Government efforts to minimize this desperation. Food for the poor : My wife called our maid yesterday to inquire about her well being and to pay some money to tide over the present situation. She replied that she can not move out of her village ( it is a small village in an urban area ) as police are enforcing the lock down strictly and only allowing those people to go out who are working for essential services. She is also working as a cleaner in a bank branch ( banks are essential services ) but has no documents to show for that, hence not allowed to go out. Same story for her husband who works as a cobbler. While they are not being allowed to go out, food is being provided by the government to all the people in this situation. That is one most essential thing which is being taken care by the state government. In case of lock down being extended, I believe this service will be continued. Medicines and Medical Services : Helpline numbers are given and they work. Medicines and hospital services are available and being made available. For all citizens, not exclusively for the poor: Being confined to home is charming maybe for a day or two. Surely not when one of the family members is in hospital and others can not move out to see him/her. I faced this situation myself. My son was at Civil Hospital, Panchkula for 4 days for testing for virus. Other 3 family members were in home quarantine. We were helped by Panchkula Police for sending clothes/ biscuits / toiletries to the hospital. Now the results have come in negative but by way of extra caution we are continuing in home quarantine. Senior Citizens living alone can call the helpline and food/medicine are delivered at home. Police and the health department workers are doing a great job under very testing circumstances. What can we do for the poor? : In my younger days there was a program —- each one teach one. That program spread literacy and education among millions of rural folk who had no access to education. In the present difficult times let us adopt the policy —- each family feed one poor family. Let the government keep on doing the macro management. We can do our little bit without looking towards the government. We can select the families from among our maids, garbage collecting person, dhobi who takes our clothes for ironing, nearby vegetable vendor who is not able to ply his cart and anyone in similar occupations. Or simply contribute to the PM CARE fund. Direct action works fast and better. To Summarize : Sufferings of the poor will increase in case the lock down is extended. Government is doing its best ( sometime less than best ) to alleviate that suffering but it is a mammoth task. Let us not be too critical of the government at this time. ( I am one of the most vocal critics of the government at other times ) We should all chip in with our efforts. Poor people are not poor by choice. Whatever little work opportunities they had, have been taken away by the lock down. Let us tough it out together. Spare a thought ( rather many thoughts ) and some money for the poor. The deadly virus will surely go away one day, our good deeds shall remain with us forever. Thanks for reading. Mother Teresa Quote Image —- Google Images

Question: How has the coronavirus affected you?
Answer: EDIT 2 : ( April 10, 2020 ) Strangely, this answer was collapsed by Quora moderation few days ago. It was restored today morning after an appeal. Second set of samples is taken today and sent for testing. Result will be known by tomorrow evening. For my son, isolation and stay in the hospital continues. For all of us, the wait is becoming longer. There is no alternative but to bear with the situation. Earlier Answer: It is the morning of March 28, 2020. India is under lockdown since March 25, 2020. I am 63 year old, retired civil engineer, now a stock market freelance consultant, blogger and a contributor here at Quora. At this point of time I do not know whether I am infected or not. I also do not know whether my wife is infected or not. That status will be known in next few hours. Why the concern?: My son and daughter in law returned from Texas, USA on March 22, 2020 , the last day the flights were allowed into India. After a very long wait at Delhi Airport, they were screened and advised HOME QUARANTINE and allowed to proceed to Panchkula, Haryana where I presently live. With a lot of difficulty they could get a taxi to come to Panchkula. At the same time, I was facing a lot more difficulty with the Residents Welfare Association of the Group Housing Society where I live. Some people were of the opinion that my son and daughter in law should not be permitted to come here. We talked to the Doctor assigned to Corona Task Force, Panchkula District. She assured that home quarantine is alright and the other residents can not dictate such terms. But it would be advisable to practice self quarantine for all the 4 persons at home. Somehow the people agreed ( reluctantly ) and my son and daughter in law arrived at around 7:00 pm. Remember, it was the day of Janata Curfew. Tension Again — Police, Ambulance, Hospital: At about 9:00 pm, a police person came to our door making inquiries about the persons arriving from abroad. After ascertaining the facts about screening at the Airport, seeing the HOME QUARANTINE stamping on their hands, he told us not to worry and left. It seems some residents were not happy with his efforts and made him call the Civil Hospital. Some 30 minutes later, he came back with a para medical person in hazmat suit to take all four of us to hospital in an ambulance. After screening at the hospital, we were again sent back to our place to follow the HOME QUARANTINE. Now we had the local hospital’s signed advice document with us. Fake WhatsAPP News Next Day : We thought that the ordeal was over. It is never like this in our society. I saw a WhatsApp message in the morning: “Residents are advised not to allow people coming from other countries into their houses and neighborhoods. Last night Panchkula Police lifted two people who had come from Australia and took them to hospital where they were found positive. “ This time I sent a message to the society group that I will be taking legal action against whosoever is spreading fake news. It was retracted immediately. It appears someone reported to Police as well and very soon I had Police presence again at my door, this time to support us. They advised us to stay at home and in case of any problem call the Police and gave their phone numbers. Well done, Panchkula Police. Thanks for your efforts. Why the concern today? : I was already living under some tension. On March 26, 2020 around 10:00 pm, my son felt a mild fever. Yesterday morning, he checked the temperature around 8:00 am. It was 100 degree F Not high fever. At 10:00 am it was same 100 degree. He thought it fit to report it to the Authorities because we should not be spreading the disease. We informed the hospital. An ambulance was sent. He was taken to the hospital. Samples have been taken and sent to PGI, Chandigarh for testing. Reports will be known sometime during the day today. What Next ? If reports are negative, he will be sent back and the home quarantine continues. If reports are positive, he stays in the isolation ward and treatment begins. All 3 of us will also be going to hospital to be kept in isolation and tested. Again, we wait for the results—- Negative or Positive. This is my experience with the corona virus till today. It will change tomorrow. My request to readers : If you notice the symptoms, please report to authorities. Do not hide it. You may be fine but do not take the risk. Other lives are also at risk. I close it here as now I have to prepare for the likely visit and confinement in hospital. I will be very happy if that is not required. But being prepared is always better.

Question: Why is the current stock market crash linked to the Coronavirus? Is there a chance that it is related to something else?
Answer: Why is the current stock market crash linked to Coronavirus? Is there a chance that it is related to something else ?: Two good questions together. My answer is from India perspective but fear and greed are universal emotions so it may be relevant for other markets too. First let us look at the crash or the correction whatever we may chose to call it: From a high of above 26500, Dow Jones Index is down to 19173 in the last one month. The ferocity of the fall is alarming and reminds us of the year 2008. NIFTY 50: It is a similar story for India with the NIFTY 50 Index: In January, NIFTY made an all time high at 12430. A month ago, it was placed around 11200. Then 10000 and 9000 and even 8000 were breached before it recovered a bit and closed at 8745 on March 20, 2020. Coronavirus Impact : The greed factor had made the market to continue its bull run till January 2020. It had to cool down a little and Coronavirus became the catalyst for the correction. As more and more people got affected by the virus and it spread world over, the initial lukewarm response turned into full fledged fear. That led to the fall. Asia Markets in fact moved up 4–5% on Friday, March 20, 2020 with the news that the virus related deaths are now under control in China where it originated. Later in the evening bad news came pouring from Italy and US as more cases were reported and death toll went spirally up. The world is looking at something which seems to have no cure. Governments are taking steps based on reactions to the events. In fact no one is sure what they are dealing with. With such uncertainty comes the fear. Fear makes the market go down and at some point crash. Coronavirus has created that fear and we can say that to a major extent, the present fall in market is due to the virus impact. Other Reasons: Now I am being India specific. Even when the market was at a high two months ago, we had stocks like YESBANK, CANBK, IDEA, TATAMOTORS, IBULHSGFIN etc which were repeatedly making the lows. One day some of these stocks would go up 10% and in the next week, lose more than 20%. There were many things wrong with such companies which were hidden by the hype and hope fed on the market highs. With the big correction, these stocks fell more and the fall can now be blamed on the virus and not on the inherent poor financials, fraudulent reporting, hiding of poor quality assets etc. Other reasons in general are: Corporate profits were stagnant or declining. But market was just moving up. At some point it had to stop. Poor financials and fraudulent reporting. The likely impact on major industries where components are imported from China. China has become the manufacturing hub for the entire world. Closing of manufacturing in China leads to big disruptions anywhere, more so in India. That loss of production is now factored in and stock prices of such businesses going down. The biggest losers are the stocks in banking and financial sector. This is the sector with bloated and fake balance sheets. Most of our banks are worthless, only YESBANK was found out. And immediately government came to rescue a bank which should have been wound up after returning the depositors’ money. But we believe in perpetuating a fraud indefinitely. So it was revived by getting money from other banks. Now YESBANK stock price has gained ( for absolutely no logical reason ) and all banks who invested in this hairbrained revival have seen there stocks falling 20–30% in just two weeks. All of the above reasons would have brought the market down at some point of time, but the fear generated by Coronavirus hastened the process. To summarize: Poor corporate profits, untrue balance sheets, recession in some sectors of economy are all the logical reasons for a fall in the market. But that fall would have been gradual. For the present, we can have Coronavirus as the cause for the crash as it has brought FEAR into the minds of people. Fear is the key. The worst is not over. The Coronavirus saga continues —- unfortunately. Stay calm, stay safe. Take precautions against the virus spread by practicing isolation. Take precautions for your trades and investments by suitable hedging. Thanks for reading. Images : Yahoo Finance

Question: What advice would you give to someone who wants to become a successful trader?
Answer: What advice would you give to someone who wants to become a successful trader? : Advising someone is a tricky task. More so in trading. I believe the question pertains to stock market trading and not to general trading in fruits, vegetables, groceries etc. Of course there is not much difference in any type of trading. Trading involves just two steps—- Buying and Selling. As long as one is able to sell at a price higher than the buying price, profit is made and one is a successful trader. Nothing could be simpler. And 90% of the traders fail in achieving this simple outcome. Failing to find success in a simple task causes doubts and we start thinking that trading is complicated. We get into theories, charts, graphs, breakouts, breakdown and spend lot of time and money to find that magic trick which will make us successful. But the outcome still remains the same. There are no profits to be seen. How to become successful? : Let us look at some other traders before we come to stock market trading. This person is a peanut seller. He buys peanuts in whole sale and sells in retail. Do we see any computers, phones, charts or graphs? No. But he makes money on most of the days while stock market traders fail to do the same. Here is another trader. He buys and sells bananas. He buys when the bananas are unripe and the price is low. He stores them, sells them when they become ripe and the selling price is higher than the buying price. This guy too makes money. People will tell me that stock market trading is different. It is not so simple as the trading shown in the above two examples. Everyone is entitled to their views but nothing could be far from truth. The above trades are actually more difficult. They have to face heat, dust and rain. They have to face the municipal authorities on the look out to remove such carts/stalls. They have to face arguments and bargaining from the customers. They have to face the problem of storing the stock securely and avoid theft and wastage. Stock market traders do not face any of these difficulties and still do not succeed in making money. Let us find out what is special about these traders ( or similar other traders) and then we bring the same to our trading. The advice: My advice to the traders is just 3 points. (1) Have the belief: Most of the traders are half hearted in their approach to trading. They neither have a plan nor an idea as to why they are trading. The traders shown in the above examples always go to the market with a belief that they will make money. Otherwise there is no point in doing the work. But do we see stock market traders with such belief and conviction? Very rarely. And it is only those rare traders who succeed. This was the first advice. (2) Know your trades: The peanut seller and the banana seller know where to buy, how much to buy, how many days to stock, when to sell, where to sell. The price is always market price. Discount may have to be given for a bulk sale but that too is market price. We also have to sell at market price in the stock market. So the playing field in similar. Only thing missing is knowledge and its application. The second advice is —- Learn whatever can be learnt about trading without getting into complication. Trading is not rocket science, it is not even basic science; but gaining some knowledge gives an edge to a trader. Never stop learning. (3) Know yourself as a trader: The peanut seller does not sell bananas and the banana seller does not sell peanuts. Both the tasks are not very difficult and can be done by just about anyone. But these people keep on doing what they do. Why? Because they are doing what they are good at. As a trader, we have to find out what we are good at and keep on doing that. We are in the market to make money, not to impress other people or to try our hands at multiple things. Find out whether you are good in cash segment or Futures/Options. Currency or commodities too can be explored. It will take some time to find your strengths and weaknesses and then it is time to define yourself as a a trader who trades successfully doing only what you do best. In my case, I found out that I am good in finding weak stocks and shorting them. Even when NIFTY has been going up and making record highs from early 2017 till now, I am buying PUT options only most of the time. And doing it profitably. The third advice is —- Know yourself. Find out what you do best. To Summarize: Trading is simple. The above three point advice will work for everyone if practiced rightly. The key is to learn from life around us. Take your stock market trading just like these two people ( peanut and banana seller) take their trading. Have the belief, knowledge and the right frame of mind. Success is bound to follow. Thanks for reading. Thanks Gurdit Kaur (गुरदित कौर) for the question. This is something I wanted to share with readers. Images : Google Images

Question: What are your top 3-4 trading rules, for example, never add to a losing position?
Answer: Some Trading Rules: The same question has been asked multiple times with some change in the wording. Basically we are looking for a set of guidelines which shall keep the losses on the lower side and make us profitable too. I have answered this few times in the past. Let us do it again but based on a previous answer which was written about two years ago. Experiences teach us and then we convert those teachings into trading rules. There are lessons to be learnt from trading. Every person is different. So lessons learnt will be different. These are my 5 rules based on trading experience over many years. Do not put all the eggs in one basket: Whether trading or investing it pays to be diversified. One can go wrong heavily in a single trade. Allocation to different stocks helps in mitigating that risk. That is why experts never tire telling you about virtues of diversified portfolio. Do not bite off more than you can chew: This is about the trade size. Never take a position in the market disproportionate to your capital in the hope of a windfall. Lotteries do exist in the market and at times you may get lucky. But more often, you will only keep chewing and not getting anything to eat. The big position size can cause a big loss which will reduce your capital and thereby your trading ability and confidence. Try not to risk more than 5% of your capital in a single trade. ( This is just an indicator figure, one has to find own comfort level ) Trade with the money you can afford to lose: ( Really ? ) The statement above is the conventional wisdom. Then there is another advice from one of the greatest masterminds: With greater risk one can look for greater rewards. But one can be wiped out as well. Markets are not one day event. The situation there is not like war. It is like daily skirmishes where you will be bloodied one day and be a victor next day. So do not bleed out in search of glory. There is always a next day. Learn from small losses. Occasional big loss will eventually come some day to test you. Do not go looking for it. That is asking for trouble. I am personally of the opinion that I can not classify my money as something I can afford to lose. If I classify it that way, I have already distanced myself from money and it will surely find a way to go away from me. I trade with the money I can not afford to lose. That makes me take my trades seriously. They are not for some entertainment or ego trip. Trades are there for making money. Some will go wrong, but the right ones have to make more money than the losing ones are taking away. One has to strike a balance in risking the money. The above advice is a good lesson to be learnt. Go with the trend- Trend is friend : There is money to be made by being a contrarian i.e. by going against the market trend. For that to happen you need perfect timing and a good dose of luck. For a normal good trader, it is best to follow the trend. Be a buyer when the markets are moving up and do not hesitate to be in short trades when the trend is down. It is similar to swimming with the current or against the current in a river. Do not struggle unnecessarily. But get out of the trade when the trend reverses. Patience pays: Stay with the right trades: In almost all my answers about trading ( whether day trades or positional, futures or options ) I have always emphasized on patience with your winning trades. These are the trades which will generate the surplus which shall keep you afloat. Big profits are good for the trading psyche also. One big profit should be able to take care of many small losses. I do not envy their job. They have to try to explain something irrational every day with some reasons. Well, the economy and the market are not the same thing. Let us look at NIFTY for one year: Index went nowhere from November 2018 to March 2019. Then the Elections were declared. The talk about job losses started around that time but the market did not care. It went on a climb in the hope of a second Modi Government and the high point of 12103 was achieved on June 03, 2019. ( Close at 12088) Once again, the lay offs, unemployment and jobs were the point of discussion and the market responded by shedding the gains and coming back to almost the level where it was in January/February 2019. In August 2019 , Finance Minister announced some concessions. That failed to cheer the market. On September 22, 2019 the big announcement was made about the tax rate reduction in corporate income tax. That made NIFTY rise 569 points in a single day. NIFTY reached 12021.4 on November 07 and 12034.15 on November 08 before shedding some of the gains to close at 11908.15. Reasons for the gain: Market gains are an outcome of buying action of many individuals. Many of them with lot of information, most of them just chasing the money flow. It is those followers of money who make the markets go higher than the desired levels and the same people suffer losses when the reality strikes. The last 30 days have been a ride to higher levels. Let us have a look at the stocks which had the maximum gain in this period. NIFTY has gained 5.26%. YESBANK is the top gainer with 61.04% followed by TATAMOTORS at 40.2%. At number 10, we have BAJAJ AUTO at 12.28%. All of these 10 stocks have recovered from recent 52 week lows. Nothing has changed for them except the slight change in market perception. Economy remains where it was but these beaten down stocks have come to party. A look at their 365 day gain will reveal the truth which is often hidden from the public. 8 out of these 10 stocks are losers over one year period. What Next? : Nobody knows. Making predictions is like tossing a coin. Let us just remember one fact. If the economy is actually struggling, markets can not stay at these levels. Thanks for reading. Question: What happens if I lose all the money in leveraging through super multiples in the Indian market and do not have any option to payback?
Answer: What happens if I lose all the money in leveraging through super multiples in the Indian Market and do not have any option to pay back? : The question is a little bit tricky. It is about not being able to pay off your liability in case of a big loss in leveraged trading in stock market. I do not know whether the person asking the question has done actual trading in the market on leverage or the question is hypothetical. Let us see how the trades are actually done. Leverage : Brokers allow trades on a specified margin which varies for every stock/index. Let us see with examples. Let us say one has a trading capital of Rs. 100000 and wants to trade in NIFTY futures. Margin requirements are as shown below: For a regular trade, you will be permitted to trade only 1 lot and for day trade 3 lots will be permitted. And you can not lose more than the margin amount paid because the trade will close automatically at a pre defined trigger price to protect you from undefined loss. Even higher leverage is provided but in that case, a stop loss is stipulated by the trader while entering the trade. As a stop loss is in place one can not lose all the money. Losing All The Money : Losing all the money can happen over a period of time or even in a single day one bets all his money on a single trade. But the point about not being able to pay is not valid. It is because the liability on account of the likely loss is always kept by the broker as the minimum margin. You will not be permitted to trade without this margin. Fortunately our market is better regulated than our banks where people can scam the banks and run away without worries about having to pay back. I hope this answers the question. Thanks for reading. Question: What is the logic behind an old saying in the stock market, "amateurs open the market and professionals close the market"?
Answer: Logic behind the saying —- “ Amateurs open the market and professionals close the market” : Well, we are looking for logic in the market sayings. Most of such sayings are based on experience of some successful trader/investor at some point of time. Some of them were true at that point, some of them are true today. Markets do not change much. Only ways of trading change. The logic for this saying is that amateur traders rush into the trade thinking that the earlier they get into a trade, more profit is there to be made. Professional traders wait for the price to settle, come within their price range and trading plan, then only they enter the trade. They are willing to wait even till end of the day. Most of these sayings carry the implied meaning —- Amateur ( Retail Traders ) have no chance to make money in the market as the market is controlled by professional traders with their big money. Another similar saying is: "Amateurs want to be right, professionals want to make money. Again, true to some extent. It is about wanting to do something. But do they get the desired results. Professionals too lose money. Amateurs lose in small trickles, professionals lose by the truckloads. Only it is not fashionable to talk about their losses. That will take away lot of shine away from the big professionals and the markets. Look at the portfolio of one of the big names in the market— Porinju Veliyath. Porinju Veliyath's Latest Portfolio, Holdings, News - Sep-19 And this is in just 3 months. It may be a similar story with other big names too. Question: What are some rules which a trader should not ignore?
Answer: What are some rules a trader should not ignore?: Nothing changes in the world of traders. The more the markets change, more they remain the same. We would like to believe that with the advent of technology there may be great changes in trading. Maybe there are for the big traders and the institutions. Now they can make mistakes faster. As far as a simple retail trader with modest means is concerned, nothing has changed in trading. The rules that applied 100 years ago are still valid today. Most traders do not follow them and therefore the fact that 90% of traders lose money remains unchanged. Before we come to the rules, let us talk about the three essentials of being a successful trader: Have the belief that trading is a profitable activity. Know your trades. Know yourself as a trader. The rules a trader should not ignore: (1) Buy Strength, sell weakness. Weak stocks remain weak while the strong keep going up. Do not try to buy a falling stock. It has same effect as catching a falling knife. If there is a doubt see the performance of RELCAPITAL, RELINFRA, YESBANK, PCJEWELERS, DHFL, IBULHSGIN, HEG etc over last one year. Add TATAMOTORS, IDEA and few more of this ilk to the mix and the picture is clear. (2) Never Trade out of your comfort zone. You see a good news report about a stock and talking heads on TV are gung ho about it. Normally you buy 100 shares. It looks like something too good. You buy 1000 shares. Few days/weeks/months later the share price comes crashing like a house of cards. The over trading will cause a much bigger loss than what should have actually happened. (3) Get out of losing stocks quickly. Decide a loss when entering a trade. As sure as night follows the day, losses will happen at times. The trick is to book the loss when it is small. Trading with a stop loss works. Trading based on hope and prayer keeps you hoping and praying. (4) Have a method for your trading. It is essential to have a method. Let the method decide which trade to take or leave. Let there be a method for exiting the trade too whether it is a profitable or losing exit. Method brings objective to your trade. Otherwise it is just random trades. Do not be fooled by randomness. Instead read the book by this name. (5) Take profit or loss with no emotions. Trading is about buying and selling. We have to do it repeatedly. It should be dull and boring. Once it becomes like a dull repetitive task, then you will see more of profits and less of losses. Cut out the emotions. (6) Do what you are good at. With some experience and experimentation, a trader should find about himself/herself. One must be good at something. Trading in equity, futures, options, currency, commodities whatever. Trade to your strength. Over the years I found out that I was good at identifying weakness. So I buy PUTS even in a rising market. Over last 17 months, market has made all time high few times. Even then my PUTS have given me very decent profits. From time to time I have bought PUT options in almost all the stocks listed under point (1) and those trades worked out very well irrespective of what NIFTY was doing. Find out your strengths and trade accordingly. (7) Keep a journal. Note down all the trades. Every brokerage site keeps the records. Analyze your trades every week. Do it again at the end of month. One learns many lessons from this activity. Trading is not fun. It is a serious activity. Give it the time and attention it deserves. The simple rules make money for you. But for most of the traders the rules do not mean anything. They go by experts’ recommendations and tips with not a care in the world where it takes them. Have a simple set of rules and follow them diligently. At first the losses will come down. After that profits and peace of mind will follow. Thanks for reading.

Question: Does the seller always win in options trading?
Answer: Does the seller always win in Options Trading?: I have been away from Quora for more than a month now. This question brings me back. There are many myths propagated in the market like: (a) Option Buyers do not make money. (b) Only way to make money in Option Trading is by writing ( selling) options as time always works in favour of the seller. (c) Almost 80% of the Options expire worthless. All of these are part truths. The real truth is that Option Sellers make small profit regularly for a long time only to give it back and much more in just one day/one week or one month. Only their failures are not talked about. Talking about the failures of big traders and institutions is not fashionable. Those with very deep pockets survive and continue with their trades believing the same half truths. Others who just joined the selling band wagon lose their capital and do not come back to market for few years. The same cycle repeats. I know many readers will not believe what I have just stated till they actually live this horrible experience. I have seen people make Rs. 2–3 lakhs every month for three years and then lose Rs. 3.00 Crores in a single day. This trader was profitable for 36 months and failed only on a single day. The day was September 21, 2018 when NIFTY tanked 400 points from the high point of the day and then recovered 300 points from the low. I would not like to encounter such a day. I will illustrate with another example: This is a healthy goat in a goat farm. He gets good food every day. That good food is the regular consistent profit. The goat looks healthy like option sellers look profitable. Then comes the day when the goat is slaughtered. All that good food counts for nothing. Another goat replaces this one and gets same good food every day. Again it makes consistent small gains on daily basis till the day of slaughter. Many days of consistent profits with proof to show for it followed by just one day of loss. To me Option Selling is like being that goat. About 80% Options expiring worthless: I agree that this is close to being true. But nobody works out what was the pay off in the options which ended up in the money. I have been posting my trades on my blog for last 15 months. About 62% of trades have either expired worthless or lost money. But the successful trades have made a profit of about Rs. 800000 on a deployed capital of Rs. 200000. All the trades were Option Buying trades. The details can be read here: Review of Trades - 15 Months - May 2018 to July 2019 I have no reason to believe that the option seller always wins in option trading. To Summarize: An option buyer becomes an option seller just after buying the option. An option seller is a buyer immediately after selling. To make profit, both have to get their trades right. Theories and loosely stated words do not make money. It is a trader with a belief, a method and patience to wait in a good trade who makes money. All others count for the 90% losers. You are welcome to disagree with my views but these views are based on real life observations and many person to person talks with successful and unsuccessful traders. After all markets exist because of difference in views. Thanks for reading. Image Source : Google Images

Answer: Can people really make money from options trading ? : I have been writing on Quora for more than two years now and most of the time about Options Trading. He replied— “ Give me half an hour and I will tell you.” He went away and returned in about 40 minutes and stated that he could eat 1 Kg. Laddus. He then proceeded to do it successfully. The other person asked him why it took him 30 minutes to know whether he could do it or not. His reply —-” I went to market. Bought and ate 1 Kg. Laddus to confirm whether I can do it.” Let us not bother about the humor aspect of the story. For us, the confirmation part is important. I too wanted to be sure before answering such question. Question: Why do most people lose money in the stock market despite the proven record that stocks go up in the long run?
Answer: Why do most people lose money in the stock market despite the proven record that stocks go up in the long run ? : It is a commonly accepted fact that almost 90% of the investors/traders do not make money in the stock market. The question seeks to know why this happens as markets ( stocks ) tend to move up in the long run. Before we come to finding the answers, there are some questions and review of the facts. We know that —- Hard Work is Key to Success. But we see it so often in life that many hard working people find no success in their efforts. Maybe something more is required along with hard work. Some say it is Smart Work that brings success and some attribute success to just plain old good luck. Stock Market is like life. In life there are far less successful people than there are mediocre and failed people. Same in stock markets. Principles of success in life are also as well documented as the methods of achieving success in the markets. Life and markets are both designed to test us and reward comes after we come through. That was the generalized statement like the one in the question—- Proven record that stocks go up in the long run ? Have we tested this statement to be true ? If yes, to which extent ? If it was really a true statement then the whole world knows the method of making money. Let us look at the numbers just for the last one year : Over last 365 days, markets have moved higher by 15.18%. A really handsome gain. Confirming the belief that stocks move higher though one year is not long term. But in the same period, 26 out of 50 stocks in the NIFTY Index have been losers. Even the blue chips like INOSYS and TCS have lost heavily in this period. This was for one year. Let us go back further: It is a screen shot from my trades in February 2015 : NIFTY was around 8500 at that time. Now it is 11665. A gain of 37.2% in almost 50 months. Now look at the prices of some of the stocks in the above trade chart: Canara Bank —- Above Rs. 440. Current price — Rs. 280 BHEL ————— above Rs. 270 Current Price —- Rs. 72.70. Adjusted for split : 109.05 ONGC ————— Above Rs. 350 Current Price — Rs. 156.55 Adjusted for split : Rs. 234 RCOM—————- Above Rs. 75 Current Price —— Rs. 3.35. SBI stock is slightly higher than where it was 4 years ago. So are DLF and VOLTAS. Out of 7 stocks in the above chart 4 are at a lower price today when Index is trading at 37% higher level. One stock has fallen to Rs. 3.35 from Rs. 75.00. These are the realities of market which are hidden under general statements about stocks going up with time. If 4 years is not long run, let us look at RCOM for still longer period: From January 2008 high of Rs. 844, it has come down to Rs. 3.35. I know some readers will come out that these were not good stocks. This wisdom comes to us after they have lost value not before that. These were the most sought out stocks in the year 2008. All of these were constituents of NIFTY , the same Index which has gone higher over the years. As these stocks lost value, they were moved out of the index and the stocks doing well were added. So the index keeps on moving up and these stocks remain losers in a very big way even after a very long run. There are stocks which gain big. But people get out by taking 20–30 or even 50% profit in those stocks. They do not get out of the losers at all. To Summarize : People book small profits in the stocks which later become multi baggers. They stay with the losing stocks till these become worthless like shown in the above examples. That is how and that is why most people lose money in the stock market. And more importantly: Stocks go up in the long run is just a saying not backed by facts. It is not a true statement. Question: I have been consistently losing money in the stock market, will I consistently win if I do the exact opposite?
Answer: Losing Money in the Stock Market. Will I win consistently if I do the exact opposite ? : A good question. A very good answer is already given by Gopal Kavalireddi. Let me add my two cents. Losing Money : We know for a fact that 90% of traders lose money. Another fact which is not highlighted is that most of them do not know what they are doing. They are just buying and selling stocks based on some recommendation on TV or by a broker or just good old gut feeling. I have nothing against these methods or non methods. Only two things can happen once a trade is taken. It goes right or it goes wrong. Nothing else is possible. And there is no trader who loses 100% of his/her trades. Market is fair in this regard. Even if you toss a coin the chance of being right is 50%. Most traders have right trades in the range 40–60%. There are exceptions but the average range is this. The problem is that we make less money from the right trades and lose more money in the wrong ones. This is the manner in which money is lost and trading gets a bad name. Planning to lose money : Nobody likes to lose money. That is why this kind of question comes up. After all it is a good thought to change what you are doing. It should help. Will it ? Last year, I was talking to one of my friends who has lost money consistently over the years in the market. This time he had a method to stop the losses and become profitable. Simple Method as told by him. “I will buy some good stocks , mostly NIFTY stocks. I will have a portfolio of 10 stocks in equal amount. Any stock which gives a profit of 30%, I will get out and replace with another one. I will keep holding others till they become profitable.” I listened to him and told him that he is on the way to losses once again. I will explain with an example: Let us say he was lucky to hold 5 stocks in his portfolio which gained maximum in the 365 day period. On the same analogy of toss of coin, he was unlucky too that his portfolio had 5 stocks which lost the maximum. Gainers : The top 5 gainers had a profit in the range 36–70%. But this gentleman would have got out at 30% profit from all of them and would not see the gains of 54% and 70%. Losers : Top 5 losers lost between 30–46%. But he will stay in all these trades and take these losses which average loss of 36.6%. The gain is restricted to 30% by own choice while loss is not limited and it has grown to 36%. With equal amount in every stock, this is a sure way to lose money. Money is made by staying in the right stocks and getting out quickly from the wrong choices. Will doing the opposite work ? : It will work only if a trader knows what he is doing in the first place. Then he is to find out what is being done wrong. After that correcting the method will work. But if no method is being followed, then nothing will work. I hope it helps. Thanks for reading. Images : NSE Website

Answer: What are some of the pointers to keep in mind when buying stock options ? (The answer is specific to Stock Options Buying in India ) I have been writing about Options Trading on Quora for about two years now. I write mostly about Option Buying and that too about Stock Options. I happen to be among a minority who believe that Option Buying is profitable. This question already has 34 answers and none of them actually answers the question. They instead talk about the difficulties of option trading. The above quote applies perfectly to Options Trading. It can be simple, it can be profitable. But most people lose money in the market and it is difficult to admit the fact that we lose money doing something which is simple. So the myth of option trading being complicated is invented by us . We hide behind this falsehood which has been spread for so long that it is taken as gospel truth now. And we do it to avoid the simple fact that we made wrong trades. Now let us get down to the pointers: In India, we have 200 stocks in which options are traded. Many of them have very low volumes and are to be avoided. We actually have about 60–70 stocks for effective trading. I will just tell what method I follow. (1) Look at the 30 day move of the stock and compare it with NIFTY move over same period. This tells us whether the stock is strong or weak. (2) If it is strong, we buy CALL option, if weak, we go for PUT option. (3) Before actually buying, we look at the 7 day move. If this move is conforming to the 30 day trend, we have a trade. (4) We have a trade at this stage but a very important factor is Implied Volatility. We are not going to make any money if the stock does not move fast enough. Surely it can move against us but in that case we know our maximum loss. The key is to cash in substantial profit from the right trades. (5) Look at the IV ( Implied Volatility ) of the near strikes and we take the trade only if the IV is between 30–50. At times exception can be made. (6) Strike Price should be taken at about 5% away from current price if IV is in 30–35 range. For higher IV, the strike price is to be 8–10% away. (7) I do not buy an option if at least 100 contracts were not traded for that strike previous on previous trading day. These 7 steps are enough to enter a trade. Incomplete Question : Profit is not made when buying an option. After buying it has to be sold to make money. Unfortunately, most traders are so focused on entering the trade that they do not care about exit. We live in the land of Mahabharat. Abhimanyu entered the Chakravyuh but could not exit. He died. So do poor traders. They do not know to plan an exit. As I have answered similar questions earlier, there is no point in repeating. Question: What are your thoughts about surge/ variable/ differential/ flexible/ dynamic pricing introduced by Indian Railways?
Answer: My thoughts about surge/flexible/dynamic pricing introduced by Indian Railways: The first thought that comes to mind: Elephants can not dance. Indian Railways tried to learn the dynamic fare dance as practiced by the Airlines. But due to shear size and ineptness it could not be agile and nimble footed. It was meant to garner some additional funds by selling some seats at a premium. But then like all things government, it was messed up during planning stage itself. Let us not get into the fare structure and all. Proof of pudding is in the eating and let us see how it is working out. Rajdhani Express Bangalore- New Delhi today ( 30–12–2018 ) : This was the availability status some 20 minutes ago. Train departs today evening. Seats available in AC 2 Tier Class — 20. Fare is Rs. 5790 which includes dynamic fare of Rs. 1682. So far so good. If one wants to travel to New Delhi today evening, we know what is the price. Railway have a TATKAL scheme too. Let us see the TATKAL booking position. Here too 10 seats are available. ( This Quota is reduced now, earlier it was much higher). The fare is same at Rs. 5790. This booking is not refundable if cancelled. The problem with these kind of fares is that they are derived with the mindset of monopoly. But reality is different. There are a number of flights operating between these two cities or any other pair of two cities. Airlines have been in the dance of dynamic fares much longer and have learn their steps. Let us look at the flights leaving around the same time from Bangalore to Delhi today: Well, we see that there are 4 offers on the first look which cost us less than the AC 2 Tier Train Fare. The journey is done in less than 3 hours as compared to 33 hours in the train. You pay less and spend less time on travel. What would be the choice? Indian Railway keeps dancing but people are watching the better dancers. Who goes to watch the not so good dancers? Friends, relatives and those who get free and discounted tickets to the show. I am not saying that trains are running empty. They are full of people travelling on discounts. I too am one of them getting senior citizen discount. There are Railway Staff ( families), politicians ( in I AC which does not have dynamic fare , but these guys travel free) and other people eligible for various concessional fares. The percentage of discount travel has increased along with the dynamic fares. And people travelling to wayside cities with no big airports do not have the option of flying at cheaper prices so they have to pay through the nose for their travel. Poor Implementation : The scheme suffers from poor implementation as well. I have seen many times that trains like Hyderabad Pune Shatabdi run with as many as 400 vacant seats but still passengers had to pay inflated dynamic fares with advance booking. This is being short sighted. Railways is squeezing the few passengers who booked earlier and then let go 400 seats paying nothing. Edit : I wanted to show some example of poor implementation but could not find it immediately and posted the answer without it. Now there is an example: This is the status as of 11:23 am for HYB-SOLAPUR journey in Hyderabad-Pune Shatabdi Express for journey on 31–12–2018 ( Tomorrow): 18 seats are available ( It is a Quota for HYB SUR) with base fare of Rs. 475 and total fare of Rs. 885. Dynamic fare component is 50% of base fare i.e. rs. 238. And this is the status for the train leaving today ( 30–12–2018) after preparation of charts: After chart is prepared 04 seats are available for the same journey today. Base fare is reduced by 10% to Rs. 428. Accordingly dynamic fare component is reduced to Rs. 214. Now you pay Rs. 810 if it is booked after the chart is prepared and seats are available. Edit 2 : Let us talk about the same Rajdhani Express Bangalore- Delhi for today. Chart is prepared now. Now 55 seats are available and fare is reduced to Rs. 5245. Those who booked in the morning paid Rs. 545 extra. This is how the dynamic pricing of Indian Railway works. Fantastic. You pay more when you plan and you pay less when you book at last minute. Trying to charge extra through dynamic fares while discounting on the other hand for seats going vacant are two policies being implemented simultaneously. That is what I said about the dancing steps being too disjointed. That was what I meant by elephants can’t dance. Well, enjoy your train journeys. Be dynamic yourself and do not bother about dynamic pricing. Thanks for reading. Enjoy your Sunday.

Question: What is a harsh truth about making money from stock trading in India?
Answer: Harsh Truth about making money from stock trading in India ? : Making money from stock trading in India or anywhere else is not easy. I have gone through the other answers and find that these are mostly truths ( harsh or otherwise) about not making money. As far as making money is concerned only very few traders are able to do it. And we want to know about the harsh truth about it. It is really a tough question. I delved deep ( or not so deep) and am able to come up with the following: (1) You are lucky when you make money and stupid when you lose it: Do not expect any accolades or congratulations from friends and family when you are able to make a profit. In their minds you just got lucky. Being smart and intelligent is something people do not associate with trading. If you were lucky while making profits, you should be just unlucky when in loss. Do not expect the world to be so kind to you. Now you will be termed as stupid. No appreciation for success and full criticism for failure is a traders lot and one has to learn to live with it. (2) It is a lonely life: Try talking about your trading with parents, spouse, children, friends and all you get is a cold shoulder. Not a shoulder you can cry on in your time of despair but a shoulder which suggests to take your burden elsewhere. You can not share your success or failures. Either you get indifference or criticism. Do not expect appreciation even at the best of times. Learn to cope with the lonely trading life. (3) All the conventional market wisdom, charts and strategies do not work all the time: We get nuggets of wisdom like: 95% of traders lose money. It is a zero sum game. Option Buyers never make money. 80% of options expire worthless. Then there are charts, bands, theories and strategies which are back tested for some time and promise great rewards if followed diligently. First about the wisdom part. Even if these sayings are true to some extent so what? Why we can not be among the 5% who make money? Similar is the talk about 80% options expiring worthless. All these talks are designed to make you a sure loser. Let your mind not be conditioned accordingly. Think on your own. Think like winners. As for the technicals like charts, bands and strategies , all of them fail and fail spectacularly. If that were not the case, big traders will never lose money. And believe me they lose by the truck loads when the markets go against them. You have to live by your own methods and by control on the emotions of fear and greed. (4) Sell at a higher price than the buy price: And to conclude the topic the biggest and simplest truth of them all. Profit = Sell Price - Cost Price This is taught at elementary school level. And we forget this fact and go for complicated and convoluted methods to get to this point. No other formula for making profit has yet been invented and is not likely to be invented. Keep life simple. As we can not control the selling price ( it depends on the prevalent market condition) , let us focus on managing our losses. Once we learn how to manage the losses, profits will start coming in. To Summarize : Trading does not have social acceptance in India. Even if you run a big trading firm or are a broker, there are people looking for your failures. Do not expect respect even if you are the biggest and successful trader. Remember, you just got lucky. As for being lonely as a trader there are few remedies. Write a journal of your trades. Write a blog like I do. share your experiences here on Quora. Other traders can benefit from your insights. Here you will not get the cold shoulder but some appreciation and thanks from those who value your experiences. Do not give much thought to losers. Always plan for success and gratefully accept whatever the markets give you. Thanks for reading.

Question: Can we exercise our right on any day in index option trading and equity option trading?
Answer: EDIT : This answer was posted two days ago. Quora Moderation deleted it within minutes of posting citing this as SPAM. It is now restored after an appeal. How is this SPAM is not clear to me. Your views please. Note : The answer is specific to Option Trading in India In India, the options trades are available on few selected indices and stocks. Presently there are 201 stocks which are available for option trades on NSE ( National stock Exchange of India). In addition options are traded on NIFTY and BANK NIFTY Index. In fact most of the trades are in these two indices. Volumes in stock options are far less. A CALL buyer has a right but not the obligation to buy at the pre determined strike price. Likewise a PUT buyer has a right to sell at a strike price. In India, the options offered for trade are European Type. We denote them as CE and PE . Here E stands for European. European Options are exercised only at Expiry of contract. This means we can not exercise our option on just any day. It has to be done at Expiry only. Cash Settlement : Till very recently, all the option trades were cash settled. You do not have to exercise the option. If holding an In The Money option, the money would be credited to your account. The process of exercise and settlement was done at the broker and exchange end the option buyer even need not bother about the mechanism. Indices anyway have to be cash settled. Physical Settlement : To reduce speculation , the regulators have decided to have physical settlement in 46 stocks out of the 201 mentioned earlier. In these stocks, one has to exercise the option. otherwise the cash will not be credited to your account. The list is available in this link: https://www.nseindia.com/content/circulars/FAOP37594.pdf To Summarize : In India, we trade European Options and the settlement mechanism is cash based not exercise based. Only in case of 46 stocks, we need to exercise the option. Thanks for reading.

There are few cases of change in religion but mostly our nationality and religions are due to accident of birth and not out of choice. And we make such a big deal out of it as if it was an achievement. Nehru Gandhi being secular does not matter at all. It is their political views which matter because they are in politics. Otherwise that too would be irrelevant. On a lighter note, I was born on Christmas Day in the building of a Mosque in a Hindu family. Could anyone be more secular ? Does it matter? Views of the masters must prevail over the view of those who have chosen to serve.
